name: James Casey
caption: The diary's first-person narrator: a former SWF midcarder whose career ended when Rip Chord tore his knee in a drunken match, who retired to North Carolina and is called back to be MAW's road agent, where he books the shows, handles the contracts and fines misbehaving staff a quarter of their pay for the local orphanage. In September 2010 he walks to the ring to his old SWF entrance music, for only the second time in nearly three years, to introduce Steve Flash as Jay Chord's challenger, and at Fall Of The King he announces that the Board of Directors has ordered Aaron Andrews's Heavyweight title match. He is visited at home in a storm by Katie Cameron after her split from Jacob Jett, takes her to dinner on New Year's Eve 2010, and fines Jay Chord for the locker-room fight; he refuses Richard Eisen's offer of the SWF's head booker's job in March 2011 and is attacked by Rip Chord in April. Rip Chord turns on him in the summer of 2011: he sits in his chair and blames him for Jay's injured elbow, hires sixteen workers behind his back and, in July, orders Jay onto commentary in his place, which the narrator takes as Rip phasing him out. After the dog dirt in a cap at Summernova he asks Steve Flash, Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole to be his ears and eyes in the locker room; he signs Ernest Youngman at $800 a night, fires Jay in September, loses Heidi Brooks's contract and Erik Strong, and takes a telephone offer from Tommy Cornell to become TCW's head road agent. In the diary's pages from September 2011 he fines Jay Chord a quarter of his show fee after Fall Of The King, takes Jay off the card for All The Leaves Are Brown, and on 26th October quits when Rip Chord demands that the main event finish be reversed; after a fight in the office he breaks his cane over Rip's head, talks him round and withdraws his resignation, saying he would rather stay, with an idea for a new title. He sits in on the release of eleven workers on 1st November, books the Farewell Tour and sees Chance Fortune, Ernest Youngman, Hugh de Aske and Steve Flash leave for the SWF, considers Tommy Cornell's job offer again, argues for cutting the touring shows and for four monthly shows, and learns from tew.com that Richard Eisen admires him. In January 2012 he plans a holiday with Katie Cameron. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he hears Wanda Fish's decision to retire, faces the press after Nelson Callum's arrest, and sets out in a note on the monthly Great Lakes or South East show the plan to reach Cult status on tew.com by the end of the year, with the profits of January and February behind it. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he fines Aaron Andrews for his rumours, re-signs Hugh Lee for three months, drinks a half-pint of vodka at his desk over the loss of KC Glenn until Rip Chord screws the cap back on, and, with Rip, vows to break Richard Eisen in two; at 12:05am on a night in August he is woken by Rip's telephone call and takes an apology from Jay Chord in Los Angeles, with Katie Cameron beside him; he writes that he would cry if Kirk Jameson did not re-sign with North of the Border Pro Wrestling, and explains the storyline he had planned for Sienna LeNoir and Black Eagle.

name: Rip Chord
caption: MAW's owner, a former SWF and TCW star who was fired from SWF for turning up drunk, now sober and talking the narrator into running his shows; he sits on commentary beside Marv Earnest, wins the October 2008 battle royal and admits he has a son. In January 2009 his son turns out to be Kid Arachnid and beats him down with Rip's own DDT; Rip is off the shows for five months, comes back at Summer Showdown refusing to get in the ring with his son, and at Iron in August 2009 agrees to a war games match on one condition. At Where It All Begins Again in October 2009 he beats his son Jay in a short brawl, finishing him with a chair; the narrator then tells both of them to stay away from the next show, makes Rip answerable for Jay's behaviour in December, and by April 2010, after Jay agrees to re-sign, Rip is standing beside his son and arranging his opponents. Through the summer of 2010 he keeps choosing Jay's challengers and refuses Aaron Andrews's title shot five times, until the Board of Directors overrules him at Fall Of The King in September and orders the match; at Where It All Begins Again in October he rings the bell to stop Andrews's pinfall in the Iron Man match, and Andrews answers by flattening him with a plancha and hitting him between the eyes with the bell. After the night of Remember November in November 2010 he tells the narrator at 3:42 am that he will talk to Jay about a new contract, proposes Matthew Gauge as Aaron Andrews's opponent at Season's Beatings, and announces the Heavyweight title rematch that the Board of Directors has granted Jay, which Jay makes a street fight at New Year, Old Rivalries in January 2011, the match the narrator calls MAW's best ever; he hands Kirk Jameson the Invitational trophy. Through the winter he presses the narrator to push Casey Valentine and Antonio, and in April, told that Jean Cattley is leaving for the SWF, he wrecks the narrator's office and drives him into a wall before walking out. Through the summer of 2011 he turns on the narrator. He sets up the Gold Rush main event for High Noon, in which the three singles champions and three "randomly drawn" opponents contest the Heavyweight title; after Jay's elbow is hurt in the match with Kirk Jameson at Mother, May I? he sits in the narrator's chair, blames him for it and wants Jameson punished, and thereafter lets Jenna carry the messages between their offices. In June he interviews sixteen cheap workers for the touring shows over the narrator's objection ("I own this company"), signs twelve at $200 a night or less and pays for them to join the Tri-State tour show out of his own pocket. At Summernova on 12th August he lifts the narrator off the floor in the dark and tells him not to threaten Jay; in September, when the narrator fires Jay for attacking Hugh de Aske, the diary leaves his answer for a later page, Rip standing behind Jay's chair days afterwards and saying that his son has turned down WLW, INSPIRE and SAISHO and expects his loyalty to be rewarded. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he takes off his headset to stand at ringside for his son's match with Randy Bumfhole and turns his back on Jay when Jay loses. After Jay's contract runs out he demands that the narrator reverse the main event finish of Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011; when the narrator quits the two fight in the office until the narrator breaks his cane over Rip's head, after which Rip admits that he wants Jay to be proud of him and the narrator talks him out of trying to be Richard Eisen. He agrees to sign no one new for a year, retires the Trios titles at Eleventh Hour on 12th November and creates the All Action title, plays Freecell in his office, stays at the announcers' table through the departures to the SWF, and agrees in late December to drop the touring shows for a month or two. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he makes the All Action title match at Leap Into The Unknown a straight wrestling match, brings back the Gold Rush match with every champion in it, sets a submission match, a ladder match and a two-out-of-three-falls match for the All Action title, announces Jim Force as Aaron Andrews's challenger at March Madness, puts the All Action and Heavyweight titles on the line together and signs Steve Gumble a couple of hours before South East Crisis so that he can take Andrews's open challenge. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he takes charge of the Smith & Singh against Second Sons match at Beach Blast, announces Kid Toma as Aaron Andrews's challenger, introduces Rudy Velasquez at Summernova on 5th August, forces Andrews to accept Rich Money's challenge and declares at Iron on 12th August that the All Action title can change hands anywhere; with the narrator he plans to break Richard Eisen in two when the day comes.

name: Jay Chord
caption: Rip Chord's grown son, who comes to MAW for one meeting with the narrator and turns down a contract because he wants to wrestle in Japan. The diary then brings him back: Kid Arachnid is unmasked as Jay at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2009, and he spends the following months as a heel main eventer at war with his father, with the Gauge Brothers and Darryl Devine at his side. He loses the October 2009 match to his father's chair, cashes in the Rip Chord Invitational title shot to take the Heavyweight title from Steven Parker in January 2010, keeps it against Thom Morgan, Stevie Grayson, Amazing Fire Fly and Kirk Jameson, fights Aaron Andrews to a time-limit draw, and re-signs in April 2010 after Rip rings the bell on Aaron Andrews's skull. He keeps the Heavyweight title through the summer of 2010, beating Erik Strong at Summer Showdown, the Masked Patriot at Beach Blast, Fumihiro Ota and Firebird at Summernova, Brandon Smith at Iron, Steve Flash at Back To School and Trent Shaffer at All The Leaves Are Brown, and adds the USPW Television and National titles and, for a week in September, the TCW International title. He loses the Heavyweight title to Aaron Andrews in the thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2010, by two falls to one, loses to Stevie Grayson at Eleventh Hour in November and leaves the show early. He beats Fumihiro Ota at Remember November in November 2010 and Kirk Jameson at Season's Beatings, but is fined a quarter of his month's pay after attacking Oscar Golden in the locker room, and wins the Tag Team match with Primus Allen over Aaron Andrews and Steve Flash at End Of Days that earns him a street fight for the Heavyweight title. He loses it to Andrews at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011, beats Amazing Fire Fly at the Invitational, loses to Darryl Devine in February, draws with him that month, beats him in March and beats Steve Flash at March Madness; the narrator notes in March that he has become USPW World champion. At Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 he calls out the new Kid Arachnid, who is wearing his old mask, and wrestles him to a draw; he has turned down 4C and EX2010, tells the narrator in e-mails that he fears being shoehorned into the feud between The Firm and the Second Sons, refuses Erik Strong's offer of an alliance and teams with him to beat Steve Flash and Arachnid on 12th May. He beats Kirk Jameson at Mother, May I? while hurting his elbow, is counted out of the six-man Gold Rush match at High Noon, draws a fifteen-minute Traditional title match with Hugh de Aske at Hotter Than Hot, beats JD Morgan at Beach Blast and in July is put on commentary, in the narrator's place, at Rip's order. He leads the Second Sons' six-man win at Summernova, plants dog dirt in Stevie Grayson's old cap, loses to Hugh at Back To School and attacks him in the locker room, for which the narrator fires him. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he stands in the ring and says he has been misguided, offers Randy Bumfhole a Heavyweight title shot for a win and loses to the Bumfhole Buster while his father turns his back on him; after the show he argues with Flash Savage and the narrator, who cannot fire him, takes a quarter of his show fee. He does not appear at All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October and is gone when his contract expires (Rip Chord tells the narrator "Jay's gone"); tew.com reports in November that he left on acrimonious terms and is an SWF target, and in December the narrator learns that he has agreed to tour with INSPIRE until March. In the diary's pages for August 2012, on a late-night telephone call that Rip Chord puts through to the narrator's home he apologises to the narrator for how things played out the year before, says that he has been seeing a psychiatrist in Los Angeles about losing his mother and about his father's absence, that he pushes himself to live up to his father and can be arrogant and rude, and that TCW has been good to him; the narrator accepts the apology without knowing whether it is genuine.

name: Erik Strong
caption: MAW Heavyweight Champion when the diary opens, a dependable main eventer who finishes with the Strongsault, defends the belt against everyone in the first ten shows and loses it in a three-way to Jean Cattley in October 2008. He beats Jay Chord and Darryl Devine on the way to the 2010 Rip Chord Invitational final, loses it to Primus Allen, and beats Hugh de Aske in May 2010 to become Jay's number one contender. He loses a Heavyweight title challenge to Jay Chord at Summer Showdown in June 2010 with the whole of the Mid Atlantic on his side; SWF then snap him up in July, to Rip Chord's anger, and call him up in August 2010. Released by Richard Eisen, he returns at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 with a Strongsault on Jean Cattley and Kashmir Singh and names the Second Sons with Antonio and Casey Valentine; Jay Chord refuses to join them but lets him help against Kid Arachnid, and they beat Steve Flash and Arachnid on 12th May. He loses a Heavyweight title challenge to Aaron Andrews on 26th May, beats Chance Fortune at High Noon, loses to Randy Bumfhole at Summer Showdown, to Flash and Bumfhole with Antonio at Beach Blast, and beats Ernest Youngman in his Summernova debut. In September he tells the narrator that he has an offer to go back up north, warns him that Rip Chord has called a roster meeting without him, and leaves.

name: Jean Cattley
caption: The company's veteran, leader of The Firm, who beats and ambushes anyone who resists it, finishes with the Mood Swing and wins his second MAW Heavyweight Championship from Erik Strong in October 2008. He fights Steven Parker to a time-limit draw at Fall Of The King in September 2009 and loses the Heavyweight title to him in an Iron Man match a month later; with Darryl Devine and Ryan Powell he wins the first MAW Trios titles for The Firm at March Madness in March 2010. The Firm loses the Trios titles at Hotter Than Hot in July 2010, and at Summernova he tells Casey Valentine that only he speaks for the group. He beats Kirk Jameson at Fall Of The King and the Masked Patriot at Back To School, and at Where It All Begins Again in October beats Valentine for control of The Firm, after which Primus Allen and Jared Johnson leave and he expels Valentine. He beats Joey Poison in a qualifier at Remember November in November 2010 and teams with Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh against Poison and the Canadian Blondes at End Of Days, then wins the Tag Team titles with Singh at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011. He loses a semi-final to Hugh de Aske at the Invitational, keeps the belts against Antonio & Raphael, the Blondes and Thrash and Firebird, beats Flash Savage at March Madness, and in April 2011 tells Rip Chord and the narrator that, at 33, he is taking a deal with the SWF. At Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 he and Singh lose the Tag Team titles to the Canadian Blondes, he refuses Casey Valentine's offer of an alliance and loses a Loser Leaves Town match to him after a Sweet Sweet Heartbreak, and after a celebration with Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole he says goodbye to the narrator in the car park after six years, handing Steve Flash the legacy of The Firm. The SWF calls him up in May with plans to revive his Mean Machine mask gimmick; by July he has lost to Kurt Laramee and been on the losing side of a four corners match.

name: Oscar Golden
caption: One of the Canadian Blondes and tag champions, who finishes with the Golden Shower and loses the MAW Tag Team titles in the Beach Blast ladder match. With Flash Savage the Canadian Blondes beat the Bailey Boys at Summernova in August 2010, win the Tag Team titles for a record third time at Fall Of The King in September and keep them in the four-team ladder match at Where It All Begins Again in October. He fights Jay Chord in the locker room after Season's Beatings in December 2010 and the Canadian Blondes lose the Tag Team titles at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011; he beats Brandon Smith at Leap Into The Unknown with the Golden Shower. He pins Jean Cattley with the Golden Shower at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 to win the Tag Team titles with Flash Savage, and the two are brought home drunk, with the belts, by two policemen who are MAW fans. Jay Chord's shouting at him is quelled by the narrator; the Blondes boast on 12th June of being four-time tag champions, debut the O, Canada! on Marshall Dillon at Summer Showdown and use it on Aero at Iron, and he loses a tour match to Jonnie Perez on 25th September. In the diary's pages from June to August 2012 he is a Canadian Blonde who pins Kashmir Singh with an O, Canada! at South East Grand Parade on 9th August.

name: Flash Savage
caption: The other Canadian Blonde and tag champion, a technical worker with a Savage elbow drop from the top. Trent Shaffer's Heart Burn pins him at Back To School in September 2010; he and Oscar Golden then win the Tag Team titles for a record third reign at Fall Of The King, and at Where It All Begins Again in October he climbs a ladder to retrieve the belts and keep them. A prank by referee Bret Graveson on him backfires on a November tour show. He pulls down the top rope on Brandon Smith at Remember November in November 2010 and wins with the Canadian Crab at Season's Beatings; the Blondes lose the Tag Team titles to Cattley and Singh at New Year, Old Rivalries. He wins the Tag Team titles with Oscar Golden at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, locks Kashmir Singh in the Canadian Crab to keep them in the Mother, May I? three-way and joins the defences through the summer; he loses to Ernest Youngman on the 18th September tour show. At Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March 2012 he brawls with the larger Brandon Smith, tires, and is finished by Smith's Backdrop Driver; at Third Time's The Charm he is drilled by KC Glenn's Tune Up The Sunshine Band.

name: Hugh Lee
caption: A Canadian Blonde who watched a Bruce Lee marathon, announced he was no longer Huey Cannonball but Hugh Lee, and spends the diary Ninja-ing in until the Blondes lose patience with him and Fumihiro Ota befriends him. He loses to Antonio on the 11th May tour show, is named by the narrator among the expendables for his $600 fee, beats VIP Wallace on 25th August and loses to him on 25th September. name: Antonio
caption: A cheating Italian heel, winner of the Rip Chord Invitational with the Italian DDT, who signs an extension, hires an assistant and takes Citizen X's money. He beats Fumihiro Ota in a qualifier at End Of Days in December 2010 and has his best match in the Invitational quarter-final against Kirk Jameson, but his contract comes up for renewal in February 2011 with Rip Chord pressing for a push, he loses a Tag Team title match with Raphael at Leap Into The Unknown, and at April Showers loses to Amazing Fire Fly and tells the crowd, "That's it – I'm done. We're done. Soon, everything's going to change..." He joins Erik Strong and Casey Valentine in the Second Sons at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, losing with Strong to Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole, and beats Joe Benning, Hugh Lee, Riley McManus and Kashmir Singh on the May tour shows. He wins with Valentine over Bumfhole and Kid Arachnid on 26th May, ambushes Bumfhole backstage at High Noon and holds him to a time-limit draw, loses to Steve Flash at Hotter Than Hot and with Strong to Flash and Bumfhole at Beach Blast, and pins Joe Benning with the Italian DDT at Back To School; Black Eagle's rumours about him earn Eagle a warning from the narrator. In the diary's pages from March to May 2012 he pins Max Mayhem at Third Time's The Charm, loses to Kashmir Singh's Bombay Duck at March Madness and beats Singh with an Italian DDT at Mother, May I? on 12th May; the narrator says he is on the roster out of loyalty to Rip Chord, and that Aaron Andrews's joke at his expense backstage was the third in five months. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he is drawn with Casey Valentine into a conversation with Father Johan in The Fallen locker room at Summer Showdown on 12th June, and the narrator tells him after the show that he has had one good match in six months, that Black Eagle has earned the title he would like and that he is still young enough to make it; he and Casey beat Smith & Singh at Beach Blast and lose at South East Grand Parade and Iron.

name: Casey Valentine
caption: A Firm heel favoured by Rip Chord, half of C-V-2 with Cameron Vessey, who finishes with the Sweet Sweet Heartbreak and has a gong-banging match with Fumihiro Ota. With Jared Johnson he keeps the Tag Team titles against the Internet Favourites at Beach Blast in July 2010, Morgan & Benning at Iron and a three-way at Back To School, and loses them to the Canadian Blondes at Fall Of The King in September. Jean Cattley accuses him at Summernova of trying to take over The Firm; injured, he and Johnson lose to Morgan & Benning at All The Leaves Are Brown, and at Where It All Begins Again in October he loses to Cattley for control of the group, Primus Allen and Jared Johnson turn on him and Cattley expels him. Rip Chord and the narrator keep him on after he snubs a move to CGC; he loses to Kirk Jameson in a qualifier at End Of Days in December 2010, is named as a possible cut in the tew.com rumours of January 2011 and wins several tour shows in February and March, the narrator saying he plans a push for Valentine around the summer. He returns at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, tells Jean Cattley that he is better than ever, and beats his old mentor in a Loser Leaves Town match with the Sweet Sweet Heartbreak; he names the Second Sons with Erik Strong and Antonio. He beats Randy Bumfhole and Kid Arachnid with Antonio on 26th May, loses to Steve Flash at High Noon and again at Summer Showdown, which the narrator calls his best match in MAW, upsets Kirk Jameson at Hotter Than Hot and Brandon Smith at Beach Blast, wins the six-man at Summernova with Jay Chord and Antonio and beats the Young Americans with Antonio at Back To School. In the diary's pages from March to May 2012 he loses to Kirk Jameson at Great Lakes Crisis, insulting Katie Cameron beforehand, wins with Antonio against the Internet Favourites at Third Time's The Charm, loses to Smith & Singh at March Madness and May The Force Be With You, wins the three-way at Spring Fever by pinning Marc Speed and beats Brandon Smith at Great Lakes Madness. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he is caught with Smith's Inverted Piledriver in the three-way at High Noon on 5th June, beats Team Honor with the Sweet Sweet Heartbreak at Summer Showdown on 12th June, where he and Antonio are drawn into The Fallen's locker room by Father Johan, and beats Smith & Singh at Beach Blast; his team loses at South East Grand Parade and at Iron on 12th August.

name: The Masked Patriot
caption: A flag-waving face and the defender of truth, justice and the American way, who feuds with Citizen X for most of 2008 and works a flying tackle and the Backdrop Driver. In February 2010 he stakes his mask on a match with Primus Allen and loses; at March Madness in March 2010 he unmasks as former NFL star "Bulldozer" Brandon Smith, hands the mask to a fan, Masked Patriot #21, and carries on under his own name, beating Jean Cattley at Spring Fever and being left out cold by Ultimate Phoenix's chair. At Summer Showdown in June 2010, still the Bulldozer, he teams with Kashmir Singh to beat Ricochet & Sharp and is then chaired by the unmasking Firebird, his former partner in The Watch; with Fumihiro Ota and Singh he wins the Trios titles at Hotter Than Hot and keeps them at Summernova. At Iron in August he challenges Jay Chord in his main-event debut and loses to the Cradle Piledriver, partners Aaron Andrews at Fall Of The King, and at Where It All Begins Again in October beats Firebird with an Inverted Piledriver after pleading with his friend to give up the darkness. At Remember November in November 2010 Brandon Smith loses the Tag Team title match with Kashmir Singh when Flash Savage pulls down the top rope; the Trios titles go at Season's Beatings, and at End Of Days the Canadian Blondes demolish him with a spike piledriver after he and Singh win with Jean Cattley. Injured, he misses New Year, Old Rivalries, returns to lose to the Blondes at the Invitational, loses to Oscar Golden's Golden Shower at Leap Into The Unknown in February, beats Jefferson Stardust, Greg Ford and VIP Wallace on tour shows, loses to Primus Allen at Third Time's The Charm and then spears Flash Savage to save Cattley and Singh from the Blondes. As Singh & Smith he loses the Tag Team title three-ways of May and July 2011, Ford & Speed at Summernova, where they tease him about the straw-blonde hair he got from a stupid bet, and beats Team XDW at Iron with Singh; he beats Jared Johnson and Curtis Jenkins and loses to Greg Ford on the tour shows, signs to tour with EX2010 in June, and loses to Casey Valentine at Beach Blast after warning him about injuring his friend Kirk Jameson. At Back To School he, Singh and Fumihiro Ota beat the Canadian Blondes and Raphael. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he loses a Tag Team title three-way and a Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews, and at All The Leaves Are Brown Providence, whom he had mentored, beats him; with Kashmir Singh he wins the Tag Team titles at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October and keeps them to the end of January 2012. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 Brandon Smith beats Providence at All Or Nothing on 12th February, beats the Canadian Blondes with Kashmir Singh at Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March, loses to Aaron Andrews for the Heavyweight title at Third Time's The Charm, enters the Gold Rush match at April Showers, loses to Casey Valentine at Great Lakes Madness and beats Marc Speed with an Inverted Piledriver at Mother, May I? on 12th May. As Brandon Smith, the Bulldozer, in the diary's pages from June to September 2012, he and Kashmir Singh keep the Tag Team titles in the three-way at High Noon on 5th June, Smith catching Casey Valentine with the Inverted Piledriver, say they have held the belts for eight months, and lose them to the Dark Raptors at Summer Showdown on 12th June. They lose to Always Breakin' Hollywood at Hotter Than Hot, to the Second Sons at Beach Blast, to the Canadian Blondes at South East Grand Parade and to Ford & Speed at Back To School on 5th September, where they sing with Sienna LeNoir, tell her she does not have to fetch his coffee and, with Donnie J, stand between her and Black Eagle.

name: Jefferson Stardust
caption: A mink-coated rock-star gimmick with an entrance as long as his matches, first with the valet Kristen Pearce and later with the manager Jakki. He beats Amazing Fire Fly with a Star Burst at Hotter Than Hot in July 2010 and then teams with Findlay O'Farraday and Kristen Pearce as Glamour And Devastation. The narrator notes that at April Showers in April 2011 he is mostly hiding behind Findlay O'Farraday. Three and a half years after his arrival the narrator still calls him awful and lists him among the expendables for $150; on the tours he beats Matt Hocking and Ben Williams and loses to Max Mayhem, Kid Arachnid, Amazing Fire Fly, Ernest Youngman and Daredevil Aero.

name: Kristen Pearce
caption: Jefferson Stardust's first valet, who takes his mink coat at the Invitational and whose contract runs out before Mother, May I?. From July 2010 she manages Glamour And Devastation, Jefferson Stardust and Findlay O'Farraday. In April 2011 Findlay O'Farraday is driven by the wish to impress her. On 5th January 2012 she appears with the Canadian Blondes at New Year, Old Rivalries, sneering at the Internet Favourites' Dawn that she is not a lady. At Summernova on 5th August 2012 she is the Canadian Blondes' manager, and the narrator calls her the star performer of the match with Spectrum Infinity.

name: Citizen X
caption: An anarchist heel who flattens the Masked Patriot with a cowbell and the Flaming Anarchy; out of character a shy man, he leaves MAW for a development deal in Rhode Island in September 2008. He returns to MAW from the SWF at Eleventh Hour on 12th November 2011 after three years away with a speech about the lie of democracy and beats Riley McManus with the Flaming Anarchy. Aaron Andrews cuts up his shoes in a prank and is dressed down by the narrator; X teams with Providence at Remember November, loses to Wanda Fish at Season's Beatings and to Kid Arachnid at End Of Days, and on 5th January 2012 loses with Firebird to Smith & Singh, Brandon Smith finally beating him. In the diary's pages from February to April 2012 he beats Wanda Fish and Thea Davis with Raphael at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, loses to Kirk Jameson at All Or Nothing and to the newcomer Donnie J at April Showers on 5th April. In the diary's pages from June to July 2012 he is the third man in the three-way for the All Action title at Summer Showdown on 12th June, betraying Eddie Powell and losing to Donnie J's Death On Miami Beach, hears Firebird's talk of falling until KC Glenn takes Firebird down, and at Beach Blast on 12th July loses to Steve Gumble's Savate Kick after printing anarchist leaflets in which Gumble says "anarchy" is spelled with a "p". The narrator says that his contract runs out shortly and that he will not renew it; the August news says that he has signed with CZCW.

name: Kashmir Singh
caption: A technical all-rounder who partners the Masked Patriot against Citizen X and finishes with the Cal-Cutter. He and Brandon Smith beat Ricochet & Sharp at Summer Showdown in June 2010; with Smith and Fumihiro Ota he takes the Trios titles from The Firm at Hotter Than Hot in July and keeps them at Summernova and Eleventh Hour. He loses to Firebird at Iron in what the narrator calls his best match in the company, and beats Sharp with the Bombay Duck at Fall Of The King and again at Where It All Begins Again. He and Brandon Smith lose the Tag Team title match with the Canadian Blondes at Remember November in November 2010, lose the Trios titles with Smith and Fumihiro Ota at Season's Beatings and, after Smith is hurt by the Blondes, bring in Jean Cattley as his partner and win the Tag Team titles at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011, keeping them to the end of April. With Cattley he loses the Tag Team titles at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 and is thrown to Antonio's Italian DDT; paired again with Brandon Smith as Singh & Smith, he comes back from a Broadway trip in pink boa, blonde hair and sequins for Hotter Than Hot, loses the title three-ways at Mother, May I? and Hotter Than Hot and to Ford & Speed at Summernova, and joins Smith and Fumihiro Ota to beat the Canadian Blondes and Raphael at Back To School. On the tours he beats Roderick Remus and Jared Johnson, loses to Antonio and Jared Johnson and, billed as "Sensational Singh", beats Raphael. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he loses to Aaron Andrews for the Heavyweight title in a twenty-one-minute match at All Or Nothing on 12th February, loses to JD Morgan for the All Action title at Third Time's The Charm, enters the Gold Rush match at April Showers, beats Greg Ford at Great Lakes Madness and loses to Antonio at Mother, May I? on 12th May. The narrator reports that he has re-signed with NYCW. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he and Brandon Smith keep the Tag Team titles in the three-way at High Noon on 5th June, lose them to the Dark Raptors at Summer Showdown on 12th June when Firebird pins him, lose to Always Breakin' Hollywood at Hotter Than Hot, to the Second Sons at Beach Blast, to the Canadian Blondes at South East Grand Parade, where Oscar Golden pins him after an O, Canada!, and to Ford & Speed at Back To School; at Back To School he sings with Sienna LeNoir, tells her she should go to New York for Broadway and the song writers he and Smith know, and stands with Donnie J between her and Black Eagle.

caption: A wrestler who runs to the ring shouting "Leeeroooyyy!!!" and wins an undercard match with it. name: Findlay O'Farraday
caption: A six-foot-eight, 350-pound monster who challenges Erik Strong in February and teams with Citizen X. At Beach Blast in July 2010 he accidentally boots his sometime partner Primus Allen while trying to save him from defeat, and Allen boots him in the head backstage and drops him; Jefferson Stardust and Kristen Pearce adopt him as the heavy lifter of Glamour And Devastation. At April Showers in April 2011 he wins for Glamour And Devastation with a Choke Sleeper on Max Mayhem, the narrator saying he is driven by a wish to impress Kristen. In June 2011 he asks for $500 a show, saying that he has been on a main show once in eight months and gets more reaction than Jefferson Stardust on tour, and the narrator refuses, offering $400; he leaves.

name: Joe Benning
caption: A fan who vaulted the guardrail to answer Findlay O'Farraday's challenge and was signed as "Regular" Joe Benning, Erik Strong's friend. He is billed with Matt Hocking as The Young Americans at April Showers in April 2011, after losing to Hugh de Aske for the Traditional title at Third Time's The Charm in March. He and Matt Hocking challenge the Canadian Blondes for the Tag Team titles on 12th May 2011 and he taps to the Canadian Crab; he beats Smart Mark on 11th July, Jared Johnson on 11th September and Nelson Callum on 18th and 25th September, is pinned by the Sweet Sweet Heartbreak at Summernova and by the Italian DDT at Back To School.

name: Kirk Jameson
caption: A talented debutant who refuses to be pushed around by Jean Cattley and The Firm and pushes Cattley to the limit in August. He and Jonnie Perez lose to Roderick Remus and Jean Cattley at Summernova in August 2010, he beats Hugh de Aske with the Bullseye at Iron, loses to Primus Allen at Back To School, to Jean Cattley at Fall Of The King and to Firebird at Eleventh Hour in November, and signs a new contract in September at $1,500 an appearance, up from $600. He loses to Jay Chord at Season's Beatings in December 2010, beats Casey Valentine in a qualifier at End Of Days and Joey Poison at New Year, Old Rivalries, and on 21st January 2011 wins the Rip Chord Invitational by beating Antonio, Firebird and Hugh de Aske in the one night. He teams with Aaron Andrews, who advises him to believe in himself, beating Ford & Speed at Leap Into The Unknown; is pinned by Thrash with JD Morgan at Third Time's The Charm, draws with Morgan at March Madness and beats Robert Thomas at April Showers. The narrator learns in February that Rhode Island has approached him. He and Aaron Andrews beat Firebird and Black Eagle at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, loses to Jay Chord at Mother, May I? in a match that injures Jay's elbow and brings Rip's wrath on him, and turns down Firebird's offer that he "consider" the dark. Betrayed by Andrews at High Noon on 12th June and again at Summer Showdown, he is hurt with a gashed forehead and then a knee injury; he loses to Casey Valentine at Hotter Than Hot, returns at Iron on 26th August, driving a Corvette, to beat JD Morgan with the Bullseye, and beats Providence at Back To School by driving his skull into the exposed turnbuckle, Firebird noting that he is "coming along quite nicely". At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he drags Rip Chord across the announcers' table to demand Firebird, beats Black Eagle, and at All The Leaves Are Brown beats Firebird with a snap DDT and a brainbuster, drops the ring bell rather than strike him and wins with a cradle, then apologises to Brandon Smith and to Aaron Andrews and offers him his hand; Andrews refuses and Jameson cashes in the guaranteed shot of the Invitational title for Where It All Begins Again on 26th October, where Andrews beats him with a Twisting Face Crusher. Firebird says that the Fall has failed; Jameson becomes Kid Arachnid's replacement mentor, is beaten down by Lockdown and by Jared Johnson at Season's Beatings, teams with Randy Bumfhole and Fumihiro Ota at End Of Days and with Bumfhole at New Year, Old Rivalries (Bullseye on Nathan Coleman), and loses to Primus Allen for the Traditional title at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he beats Black Eagle with the Kirk-Hold at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February after refusing the advances of Sienna LeNoir, Citizen X at All Or Nothing and Casey Valentine at Great Lakes Crisis, with Katie Cameron now his manager, loses a submission match for the All Action title to JD Morgan at March Madness, beats Providence at April Showers, is stomped by Primus Allen afterwards, and beats Lord Geoffrey Windameer at Spring Fever on 12th April, where he promises to cleanse the company of Firebird, Black Eagle, Providence and his old friend Aaron. He and KC Glenn lose to Firebird and Father Johan at Mother, May I? on 12th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he loses to Firebird at High Noon on 5th June, draws with a clown-faced Providence at Summer Showdown on 12th June and warns Aaron Andrews about The Fallen's recruiting, only for Andrews to hit him with the Heavyweight belt, which puts him in hospital for a month. He returns at Beach Blast on 12th July to name the Knights Templar and beats Raphael with The Bullseye, teams with JD Morgan to beat Providence and The Great Ota at Summernova on 5th August and brings Rich Money, who has funded the help he has found, to the ring; he and Bradford Peverell lose to Firebird and Ota at South East Grand Parade on 9th August, he and Money beat Andrews and Ota at Iron on 12th August, and at Back To School on 5th September he beats Rudy Velasquez with the Kirkhold. The narrator renews his contract at a 20% pay cut, $2,000 an appearance for his previous $2,500, sends him to 4C in the trade that brings Money to MAW, and says he would cry if Jameson did not re-sign with NOTBPW.

name: Raphael
caption: Antonio's "personal assistant" with a Bluetooth earpiece and a Blackberry, who wrestles alongside him. A PPA deal with 4C is reported in February 2011; he and Antonio lose to Cattley and Singh at Leap Into The Unknown. He loses to Riley McManus, Kid Arachnid and Ernest Youngman and to "Sensational" Singh on the tour shows, beats Jonnie Perez and Ben Williams, is on the narrator's list of expendables for lack of direction, and joins the Canadian Blondes against Smith, Singh and Ota at Back To School. In the diary's pages from February to April 2012 he beats Wanda Fish and Thea Davis with Citizen X at Leap Into The Unknown, beats Lassana Makutsi at All Or Nothing, loses to Bradford Peverell at Third Time's The Charm and beats Amazing Fire Fly at Spring Fever on 12th April. The narrator checks his new contract in February; in May he notes that the midcarder has parted ways with the company on amicable terms. In the diary's pages from June to July 2012 he loses the High Noon six-man on 5th June to Bradford Peverell's Dream Left Hook, beats Thea Davis with an Italian DDT at South East Madness on 9th June, and loses to Kirk Jameson's Bullseye at Beach Blast on 12th July, the narrator's let-down; the narrator's news says that he has signed a pay-per-appearance deal with CGC.

name: Katie Cameron
caption: Erik Strong's manager from Beach Blast, who swats Raphael with a chair. In July 2010 she asks the narrator why he is avoiding her and he sends her to talk to her boyfriend Jacob Jett; when Jett moves to Japan in August, her friends press the narrator to comfort her, and he refuses to step in while the couple is together. She cheers Steve Flash on at ringside at Fall Of The King in September. In November 2010 she comes to the narrator's door in a storm, in tears, saying that she and Jacob Jett have split up; on New Year's Eve 2010 she meets the narrator for dinner, and in January 2011 he writes that they are doing fine. She is away with 4C when Jean Cattley leaves in April 2011, is back in town for the Beach Blast weekend, and is in the narrator's bed when Rip rings about Kirk Jameson's knee; Tommy Cornell's offer would find her a place at TCW as well. She is Kirk Jameson's manager from Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March 2012, telling Casey Valentine, who insults her, that her client will be that much more thorough in destroying him, and saying that she was aligned with Aaron Andrews until he lost the plot; she is with Jameson at April Showers and Spring Fever. In the diary's pages for August 2012 she is beside the narrator when Jay Chord telephones at 12:05am to apologise, clamps a hand over his mouth to keep him from saying something he might regret, and asks what harm accepting it can do.

name: Black Eagle
caption: A masked veteran who does not speak for himself, signed in June 2008 and managed by Sienna LeNoir, who finishes with the New Jersey Turnpike. He is beaten by Ultimate Phoenix in a Loser Leaves Town match at Fall Of The King in September 2009 and leaves the company, his contract up. Rip Chord brings him back at April Showers in April 2011 after his Loser Leaves Town defeat; he beats Jonnie Perez with the New Jersey Turnpike and Firebird, who forced him out in 2009, greets him with an embrace. He returns at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 with Sienna LeNoir at his side, loses to Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson with Firebird, loses a Heavyweight title challenge to Andrews on 12th May and the Dark Raptors three-way on 26th May, and loses to Hugh de Aske at Summer Showdown in their fight over Sienna, to Randy Bumfhole at Hotter Than Hot and to Chance Fortune at Beach Blast. Rumours he spreads about Antonio earn a stern warning from the narrator; at Iron he accepts Hugh's challenge for Sienna, loses to the Cutthroat Driver and then smashes Hugh with the ring bell as Sienna leans in for a kiss. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 Kirk Jameson beats him and he leaves on a gurney with Sienna LeNoir behind him; he fights Hugh de Aske to a draw at Where It All Begins Again for Sienna's love. With Firebird as the Dark Raptors he wins the All Action title for a few minutes at Remember November, spreads rumours about Jared Johnson that earn him a dressing down from the narrator, takes Sienna back on 26th December and loses to Fumihiro Ota in an Invitational qualifier. In the diary's pages from February 2012 he loses to Kirk Jameson at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February and is fined by the narrator for spreading rumours about Rock Downpour, is pinned by Randy Bumfhole's Bumfhole Buster when the Dark Raptors lose to KC Glenn and Bumfhole at All Or Nothing, and then has spinal surgery, the surgeon saying he should walk again in two months but that it may be a case of waiting to see whether he wrestles again, the flight from Tokyo after his GCG injury having aggravated it. In the narrator's April news his ex-girlfriend Raven Nightfall retires, and he upsets Fumihiro Ota at FCW's last show. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he returns freshly healed from spinal surgery at Summer Showdown on 12th June with Sienna LeNoir, Firebird's partner as The Dark Raptors, and the pair win the Tag Team titles from Smith & Singh; the narrator warns him, a night after his return, to stop messing about and living his gimmick, and Antonio resents the title he was handed. He loses to KC Glenn at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July and to JD Morgan at Beach Blast on 12th July, wins the All Action title backstage at Iron on 12th August with Firebird's help, only to be pinned for it the same night by Donnie J, and keeps the Tag Team titles against the West Texas Peacekeepers, the XX Factor and Spectrum Infinity. At Back To School on 5th September he taps out to Team Honor's Carolina Crossface, shoves Sienna away and is kicked by her; his contract then expires and, the narrator writes, he will not negotiate and leaves the company.

name: Sienna LeNoir
caption: Black Eagle's husky-voiced manager. After Black Eagle leaves in September 2009 she turns up at End Of Days in December on Hugh de Aske's arm, in pirate rags, and stays with the pirate through the spring. Jay Chord dances with her at the party after Iron in August 2010, and at Where It All Begins Again in October she makes out with Hugh de Aske in a backstage segment. She gives Hugh de Aske a massage before the 2011 Invitational and blocks the Masked Patriot's throw in their quarter-final; at Leap Into The Unknown in February 2011 she signs Hugh's name with a quill on the Perez and Gauge rematch contract that his cutlass has split in two. From Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 she leaves Hugh de Aske for Black Eagle, announces that her love was always with Eagle, comes to ringside with Providence and sends hypnotic messages to Kirk Jameson inviting him to join the dark; at Summer Showdown she hides a turnbuckle cover in her dress, and at Iron she seems to yield to Hugh's kiss until Eagle smashes him with the ring bell and she goes back to his side. At Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011 Hugh de Aske and Black Eagle fight for her love in a corridor and then in the ring to a time-limit draw, and she flees in tears; after Hugh leaves she returns on 26th December in her Mistress of the Night regalia to speak Black Eagle's words again. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 she tries Black Eagle's seduction on Kirk Jameson at Leap Into The Unknown and on KC Glenn at All Or Nothing, and both turn her down; with Eagle in hospital she tells Firebird at Spring Fever that she will serve him, is sent away by him at May The Force Be With You and driven from the room by Father Johan at Mother, May I?. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 she slumps like a de-powered robot in the corner at High Noon on 5th June and whispers that he will return, with Firebird at South East Madness carries the towel that ends his match, and at Summer Showdown on 12th June announces the return of Black Eagle, her master, and tries to lure Eddie Powell until KC Glenn stops her. At Back To School on 5th September Aaron Andrews sends her for coffee, Kashmir Singh and Brandon Smith sing "My Favorite Things" with her, and when Black Eagle loses the Tag Team titles and shoves her, she slits her skirt and kicks him in the groin, tells him she gave everything and got nothing in return, and leaves for the final time, urged by Singh and Donnie J to go to New York; the narrator writes that her contract expired with Eagle's and that both have left the company.

name: Fumihiro Ota
caption: A veteran ninja and former TCW Cruiserweight Champion who answers with gong bongs and smoke pellets, debuts as Max Mayhem's replacement in May and befriends Hugh Lee. With Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh he wins the Trios titles from The Firm at Hotter Than Hot in July 2010 and keeps them at Summernova and Eleventh Hour; he draws with Firebird at Summer Showdown in June, loses a three-way for the Heavyweight title at Summernova, and loses to Ricochet's Cross Armbreaker at Fall Of The King and to Toxin's cradle at Where It All Begins Again. Firebird names Evil Spirit as his former student. He loses to Jay Chord at Remember November in November 2010, loses the Trios titles at Season's Beatings and loses to Antonio in a qualifier at End Of Days. He is attacked by Firebird, Evil Spirit and Thrash in February 2011, beats Evil Spirit with the Ninja Strike at Third Time's The Charm and Primus Allen at March Madness. He loses to Hugh de Aske at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 in a Ninja versus Pirate Traditional title match, beats Jared Johnson at High Noon and JD Morgan at Summer Showdown, and loses a Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews at Hotter Than Hot. He loses with the Young Americans to Jay Chord, Casey Valentine and Antonio at Summernova and, with Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh, beats the Canadian Blondes and Raphael at Back To School; at $1,500 a show he heads the narrator's list of expendables. He loses to Providence at Where It All Begins Again, is made into Team OMGsplosion with Hugh de Aske at Eleventh Hour on 12th November 2011, loses a Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews at Season's Beatings after a Lockdown beating, teams with Randy Bumfhole and Kirk Jameson at End Of Days, and at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012 beats Providence in the first round and loses the semi-final to JD Morgan. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he loses the Triple Threat for the All Action title to JD Morgan at All Or Nothing, beats Eddie Powell at South East Crisis and Lenny Brown at Spring Fever with the Ninja Strike, and loses with Amazing Fire Fly to Primus Allen and Lenny Brown at May The Force Be With You on 5th May; the narrator notes that Black Eagle upset him at FCW's last show. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he appears backstage at South East Madness on 9th June, in the dark, to challenge Aaron Andrews, and loses the Heavyweight title match, the narrator's thirty-fourth defence for the champion, to the Twisting Face Crusher after thirty minutes, before taking off his hood in the ring and standing lost in thought. At Summer Showdown on 12th June he drops Donnie J with a Ninja Strike and joins The Fallen, painted in black and white with kanji symbols, and wishes to be called The Great Ota; he beats KC Glenn at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July and curb-stomps him, beats Amazing Fire Fly at Beach Blast on 12th July, loses with Providence to Kirk Jameson and JD Morgan at Summernova, beats Peverell and Jameson with Firebird at South East Grand Parade, loses with Andrews to Rich Money and Jameson at Iron, and draws with Randy Bumfhole at Back To School on 5th September. Andrews says he refused to join The Fallen unless Ota did.

name: Ultimate Phoenix
caption: A masked high-flyer signed in July 2008 who lectures rivals on citizenship and freedom and finishes with the Phoenix Firebird Splash. He beats Black Eagle in a Loser Leaves Town match in September 2009, leads The Watch against The Firm for the first Trios titles in March 2010, loses The Watch's series at Spring Fever in April and turns on his own side with a chair. At Summer Showdown on 23rd June 2010 he swerves a chair attack on Ricochet to chair Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh, his former Watch partners, and pulls off his blue-and-white mask to show a black-and-red one with flames: "I am Firebird!" He preaches a crusade in which a man must fall to the bottom of his soul before he can find the light, draws with Fumihiro Ota at Summer Showdown, beats Amazing Fire Fly, Kashmir Singh, Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson in the following months, and loses to Brandon Smith's Inverted Piledriver at Where It All Begins Again in October 2010. He loses to the Masked Patriot at Remember November in November 2010, beats the Internet Favourites with Evil Spirit at Season's Beatings, and in the 2011 Invitational beats Riley McManus and Steve Flash before losing a semi-final to Kirk Jameson. He beats the Masked Patriot in February, introduces Thrash at All Or Nothing and loses to Aaron Andrews for the Heavyweight title at March Madness; at April Showers he and Thrash lose a Tag Team title challenge to Cattley and Singh, and he greets Black Eagle, whom he forced out in 2009, listing Thrash, Greg Ford, Marc Speed, Evil Spirit and JD Morgan as his followers. At Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 he and Black Eagle lose to Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson; at Mother, May I? he and Black Eagle, as the Dark Raptors, lose a Tag Team three-way when Oscar Golden crotches him on the top rope, and he presents the converted Masked Patriot as Providence, tells Kirk Jameson that the path is his own and offers him a way to the dark. At High Noon the Bullseye from the top rope eliminates him from the Gold Rush; he wins with Providence at Summer Showdown, and at Back To School he and JD Morgan lead a Fallen trio against The Firm for the Trios titles and he is pinned by Randy Bumfhole's Bumfhole Buster. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he tells Kirk Jameson that his only match is against his own mentor, Black Eagle, and after losing to Jameson at All The Leaves Are Brown laughs as Jameson refuses to strike him; at Where It All Begins Again he sits alone in the dark to say that The Fallen have failed and that "from now on, we will be everywhere". With Black Eagle he is billed as the Dark Raptors, beats the Young Americans and Lassana Makutsi and Amazing Fire Fly, loses the tag three-ways, helps Black Eagle to the All Action title, and loses to Kid Arachnid in the Invitational semi-final on 12th January 2012. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he beats Randy Bumfhole at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, Bradford Peverell at March Madness and KC Glenn at May The Force Be With You, draws with Steve Gumble at Spring Fever and, with Black Eagle in hospital, takes a singles run; he calls in Father Johan as an ally, takes Sienna LeNoir's service for himself and then sends her away, and with Father Johan beats KC Glenn and Kirk Jameson at Mother, May I? on 12th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 Firebird beats Kirk Jameson with the Phoenix Firebird Splash at High Noon on 5th June, loses a submission match to Donnie J when Sienna LeNoir throws in a towel at South East Madness, wins the Tag Team titles with Black Eagle at Summer Showdown on 12th June, loses to Donnie J at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July and, with The Great Ota, beats Peverell and Jameson at South East Grand Parade on 9th August. At Iron on 12th August he throws Donnie J into crates, helps Eagle win the All Action title, and then strikes Eagle in the throat in a corridor, meaning to capitalise; at Back To School on 5th September he loses the Tag Team titles with Eagle to Team Honor, and he calls himself the leader of The Fallen.

name: Kid Arachnid
caption: A young technician in a black Spider-Man mask who debuts at Beach Blast and beats Antonio on Fall Of The King. The masked wrestler who wins The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2009 is unmasked as Rip Chord's son Jay; the diary's own housekeeping note says Thom Morgan wore the mask until just before Remember November. The Arachnid gimmick returns on the 11th April 2011 tour show, when Kid Arachnid teams with Jonnie Perez against Flash Savage and Roderick Remus; the narrator's note says it is not Jay. A new Arachnid, whom Jay Chord says is not him under the mask, wins on the 25th April tour show and is called out by Jay Chord at Spring Fever, the match ending in a draw. He becomes the fourth man of Steve Flash's new Firm, loses with Flash to Erik Strong and Jay Chord and with Randy Bumfhole to Casey Valentine and Antonio, wins most of his tour matches (Greg Ford, Curtis Jenkins, Roderick Remus, Nelson Callum, Jared Johnson, Jefferson Stardust, Extreme Deluxe) and, with Chance Fortune and Bumfhole, takes the Trios titles from The Triple Threat at Summernova on 12th August, pinning Nelson Callum with the Cradle Piledriver. At Back To School Jay Chord attacks him and tries to tear off his mask; the narrator notes that a Japanese company wants to take him on tour. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he beats Antonio with the Cradle Piledriver; the narrator says the interest is in who is under the mask. After Jay Chord's departure Chance Fortune tells him at Farewell Tour on 22nd November, when he beats Citizen X, that he does not need the mask, and Kirk Jameson becomes his mentor; at Remember November he wins the All Action title with a chair backstage and loses it within minutes, then loses a tag match to Providence and Citizen X. He beats Citizen X in an Invitational qualifier at End Of Days, loses to Primus Allen for the Traditional title on 5th January 2012, and at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January beats Jared Johnson, Firebird and JD Morgan on the one night to win the tournament, removing the mask to say that his name is KC Glenn. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 KC Glenn, the Rip Chord Invitational champion, prepares to take his bow against Primus Allen and draws with him for the Traditional title at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, beats the Dark Raptors with Randy Bumfhole at All Or Nothing, beats the Canadian Blondes with Jared Johnson at Third Time's The Charm and Citizen X at March Madness, is entered in the Gold Rush match at April Showers, and loses to Firebird and to Father Johan, who invites him to join his family, and with Kirk Jameson to Firebird and Father Johan at Mother, May I? The narrator notes that his microphone skills have grown out of sharing promo time with Rip Chord on the tours, and that he can cash in his title shot at any time. In the diary's pages from June to July 2012 KC Glenn is the new GCG Openweight champion, and the narrator thinks seriously about how he might look with the MAW title round his waist. He loses with Bradford Peverell to Ford & Speed at South East Madness on 9th June, cashes in his Invitational guaranteed title shot against Andrews at Summer Showdown on 12th June and loses after a near-standstill twenty minutes, is felled with the belt by Andrews, beats Black Eagle with a Tune Up The Sunshine Band at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July and loses to The Great Ota at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, before coming into the ring with a chair to save Donnie J and JD Morgan. At Beach Blast on 12th July he and Father Johan fall from the top turnbuckle of the lumberjack match to the arena floor and are taken out on stretchers, and the narrator says he has broken through with someone else and left MAW.

name: Shane Nelson
caption: A signing made in August 2008 for the On Tour shows. He is put down by Primus Allen's Running Powerslam in the Trios title match at Summer Showdown in June 2010; his contract expires in September 2010 and he leaves MAW, at 32 and $900 a time, with a best rating of D in his sixteen matches.

name: Stevie Grayson
caption: Trent Shaffer's new partner and tag champion from Fall Of The King, a veteran with the 460 Degree Splash. He wins the first MAW Traditional title in March 2009 and loses it to Darryl Devine at Beach Blast. He regains the Traditional title from Darryl Devine at Where It All Begins Again in October 2009, loses it to Hugh de Aske at End Of Days, wins the number one contender's final over Champagne Lover at March Madness in March 2010 and loses to Jay Chord for the Heavyweight title that night. He beats Hugh de Aske with a Shining Wizard at Summer Showdown in June 2010, with Jenny by his side, teams with Trent Shaffer from Beach Blast in July, and at Eleventh Hour in November is set up by Aaron Andrews as Jay Chord's opponent, jumps the champion as he arrives and beats him with a 460 Degree Splash. He loses to Primus Allen at Season's Beatings in December 2010 and to Matthew Gauge at New Year, Old Rivalries, and to VIP Wallace at All Or Nothing in February 2011 in what the narrator expects to be his last match for MAW, his contract not being renewed. He and Thomas Morgan are told on 12th May 2011 that this is their last chance to save themselves, complain about everything and lose to Ford & Speed's Cross Armbar; the narrator and Rip agree they are canned, and he leaves in June, his old baseball cap later turning up filled with dog dirt.

name: Jacob Jett
caption: A cheaply paid all-rounder signed in September 2008 to take Citizen X's title shot, who loses to Erik Strong on his debut. He leaves for Japan after Remember November, turns down a return in February 2009, and comes back at Summer Showdown in June as a face to challenge Jean Cattley.

name: Primus Allen
caption: "The Rookie Monster", an outsider who runs through the Masked Patriot at End Of Days in December 2008, is taken into The Firm in place of Ricky Douglas and finishes with the Running Powerslam; he beats Erik Strong at The Rip Chord Invitational and is the Firm's enforcer through 2009. He wins the 2010 Rip Chord Invitational from Erik Strong in January 2010, beats the Masked Patriot in a mask-versus-career match at All Or Nothing in February and loses to Kirk Jameson's Kirk-Hold at March Madness. At Summer Showdown in June 2010 he steps into The Firm's Trios team for the departed Darryl Devine and wrestles twice that night, scoring a pin with the Running Powerslam and losing with Findlay O'Farraday to the Bailey Boys. He boots Findlay for a misfired kick after losing to Jesse Christian at Beach Blast, beats Aaron Andrews for the Traditional title at Iron, keeps it against Kirk Jameson and Joe Benning and loses it to Jonnie Perez at Where It All Begins Again in October, then powerbombs Casey Valentine and leaves The Firm, announcing that he is after the Heavyweight title. At Eleventh Hour in November he draws with Steve Flash and says he will cash in the Invitational's guaranteed title shot on Aaron Andrews at the 2011 Invitational. He beats Stevie Grayson at Season's Beatings in December 2010 and wins with Jay Chord at End Of Days; on 21st January 2011 he spends the title shot his Invitational crown carries on Aaron Andrews and loses, having beaten the Masked Patriot at New Year, Old Rivalries. The narrator can think of nothing to do with him: he beats Brandon Smith at Third Time's The Charm and loses to Fumihiro Ota at March Madness. He returns at Summer Showdown on 26th June 2011 by ambushing Chance Fortune backstage and beating him with the Running Powerslam, squashes Jonnie Perez at Beach Blast, and at Summernova on 12th August wins the Traditional title from Hugh de Aske with a Sitout Spinebuster, a title he keeps against Ernest Youngman at Iron and Steve Flash and Erik Strong at Back To School. The narrator, who has him on a list of expendables for lack of progress, hopes to keep him happy until October, when there may be room for a storyline. He beats Bradford Peverell at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011 and Riley McManus at Season's Beatings to keep the Traditional title, partners Aaron Andrews in the loss to the Fabulous Bumfholes on 12th November, draws with Jared Johnson at End Of Days and beats Kid Arachnid on 5th January 2012 and Kirk Jameson at The Rip Chord Invitational. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he draws with KC Glenn at Leap Into The Unknown, beats Randy Bumfhole at Third Time's The Charm and Lassana Makutsi at March Madness, and loses the Traditional title at April Showers on 5th April when JD Morgan pins him in the Gold Rush match. He loses to Amazing Fire Fly at South East Crisis on 8th April, introduces his old friend Lenny Brown there and forms a tag team with him, beating Fire Fly and Fumihiro Ota at May The Force Be With You on 5th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he and Lenny Brown are introduced by Haley Buck at High Noon on 5th June as Always Breakin' Hollywood, "the future of professional wrestling", and beat the West Texas Peacekeepers and the Canadian Blondes, Team Honor at South East Madness with a Sit-Out Spinebuster on Jared Johnson and Smith & Singh at Hotter Than Hot with the same move on Kashmir Singh. At Iron on 12th August Allen and Brown lose the three-way to Team Honor and are turned away by Rudy Velasquez, who twists Allen's wrist, and at Back To School on 5th September they beat the XX Factor, Allen insisting that they take no pleasure in beating up women.

name: Matthew Gauge
caption: One of the Gauge twins, Sam Keith's sons, who debut at End Of Days in December 2008, win the MAW Tag Team titles at The Rip Chord Invitational with Lisa Bowen at their side and finish with the Depth Gauge; he stands beside Jay Chord when Jay's war on his father begins and beats Ultimate Phoenix at Beach Blast. GCG snap him up in November 2009, after Where It All Begins Again, which kills the narrator's planned feud with Stevie Grayson. Rip Chord brings him back at Season's Beatings in December 2010 to challenge Aaron Andrews; Andrews wins, and Gauge loses to Jonnie Perez at End Of Days, beats Stevie Grayson at New Year, Old Rivalries and wins the Traditional title from Perez at the Invitational. In February he tells the narrator that he is going to Burning Hammer in Japan, loses the title to Hugh de Aske at Leap Into The Unknown and leaves with a broken tailbone.

name: Greg Gauge
caption: The other Gauge twin, who signs for USPW and leaves MAW in May 2009 (Jay Chord blames Rip) and turns up again at Iron in August 2009 to help his brother beat Erik Strong; the narrator rates him too good for MAW. He leaves MAW after Where It All Begins Again in October 2009, where his creative control clause stops the finish the narrator wanted.

name: Lisa Bowen
caption: A young manager who comes to the ring with the Gauge Brothers at The Rip Chord Invitational, introduced by Matthew Gauge and named by Rip Chord as Runaway Train's daughter; at $500 an appearance she is the most expensive manager the narrator has hired, and her last appearance is set for Fall Of The King.

name: Darryl Devine
caption: A young wrestler Jay Chord brings in at Summer Showdown in June 2009 to take Greg Gauge's place; he finishes with the Devine Dream Drop, takes the MAW Traditional title from Stevie Grayson at Beach Blast and keeps it from Ultimate Phoenix at Iron. He loses the Traditional title to Stevie Grayson in October 2009, challenges Steven Parker for the Heavyweight title in November, loses to Erik Strong in the 2010 Invitational semi-final, and in March 2010 joins The Firm, whose Trios titles he helps win; the diary has Jean Cattley call him a follower who needs to be led. In June 2010 a young blond "Darryl" hands the narrator his notice because TCW are recruiting; the diary gives no surname, and Darryl Devine is the only Darryl on its roster. By Summer Showdown in June 2010 he has taken an offer from out west and left The Firm, Casey Valentine tells Jean Cattley; Cattley later blames Valentine for driving him out. He returns at Leap Into The Unknown on 12th February 2011 to accept Jay Chord's open challenge and wins with the Devine Dream Drop, saves Aaron Andrews from a beating at All Or Nothing and draws with Jay, and makes his last appearance for now at Third Time's The Charm on 12th March 2011, putting Jay over after Rip Chord's talk, the month after Tommy Cornell's orders made him balk at losing to Jay.

name: Rock Downpour
caption: A former NYCW wrestler who joins MAW in the spring of 2009 and works the commentary desk with the narrator at Mother, May I?. He introduces Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole on commentary at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, signs a contract extension in May for $100 a show less than he was otherwise on, his second pay cut, and is on commentary at Summer Showdown and Beach Blast. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 Black Eagle spreads rumours about him and is fined; he commentates at Great Lakes Madness and Mother, May I?. In the diary's pages for June 2012 he is on commentary with Rip Chord and the narrator at South East Madness on 9th June, and at Summer Showdown on 12th June he screams the name of Fumihiro Ota.

name: Hugh de Aske
caption: A piratical newcomer, also working for NYCW, who enters in a rowboat pushed by his crew; he loses a near fifteen-minute Invitational match to Stevie Grayson in November 2009, takes the MAW Traditional title from him at End Of Days with the Cut Throat Driver and keeps it against Fumihiro Ota, Hugh Lee, "Bulldozer" Brandon Smith (a time-limit draw) and Kirk Jameson, with Sienna LeNoir at his side, until Aaron Andrews wins it at Spring Fever in April 2010. He loses to Stevie Grayson at Summer Showdown in June 2010, signs a contract extension that summer, beats the Masked Patriot with the Cut Throat Driver at Summernova, loses to Kirk Jameson at Iron, and at All The Leaves Are Brown in October loses a steel-cage match to Aaron Andrews after Rip Chord promises him "a lot of booty" if he wins. At Where It All Begins Again he makes out with Sienna LeNoir in a backstage segment and then loses to Steve Flash, who reverses his Cutthroat Driver into a Flash Bang. He loses to Aaron Andrews in a Heavyweight title match at Remember November in November 2010 and, in the 2011 Invitational, beats Amazing Fire Fly, the Masked Patriot and Jean Cattley before losing the final to Kirk Jameson. At Leap Into The Unknown on 12th February 2011, after he and Sienna LeNoir cut a contract in half with a cutlass, he wins the Traditional title in a three-way with Jonnie Perez and Matthew Gauge, keeps it against Perez, Jean Cattley and Joe Benning, and, having "wised up to his true worth", is no longer available for the touring shows from March. Sienna LeNoir leaves him at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011: he beats Fumihiro Ota with the Cutthroat Driver to keep the Traditional title but runs after her, leaving the belt behind, and finds her in Black Eagle's dressing room. He is chaired by the Masked Patriot on 12th May, beats Providence on 26th May and Black Eagle at Summer Showdown, draws with Jay Chord at Hotter Than Hot, loses a Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews at Beach Blast and the Traditional title to Primus Allen at Summernova. At Iron he beats Black Eagle for the right to speak to Sienna, only to be struck with the ring bell as he leans in for a kiss, and at Back To School he beats Jay Chord and is attacked by him in the locker room. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he loses to JD Morgan, distracted by Black Eagle being wheeled out on a gurney, and at Where It All Begins Again fights Black Eagle to a time-limit draw for the love of Sienna LeNoir; at Eleventh Hour on 12th November he teams with Fumihiro Ota as Team OMGsplosion, and after losing to Lockdown at Farewell Tour on 22nd November he leaves for the SWF. Haley Buck says on 26th December that she had him fired.

name: Heidi Brooks
caption: A highly respected former women's star whom the narrator hires in November 2009 as an extra backstage presence to calm the locker room; she helps him find the way round the standoff with Rip and Jay Chord, is the narrator's "Good old Heidi" when the crowd chants at Jay at End Of Days, and spends the following months teasing him about Katie Cameron. She attends the locker-room meeting after Remember November in November 2010 and keeps the narrator informed of the roster's contract news in the winter of 2011. In September 2011 she tells the narrator in tears that Rip Chord will not renew her contract because the company is running at a loss, and urges him to take Tommy Cornell's offer and get out before Rip runs MAW into the ground; she brings ice to the narrator's office after Jay Chord's fight with Hugh de Aske.

name: Champagne Lover
caption: A long-haired Mexican luchador who comes in with a platoon of salsa dancers for The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2010 on his way to Canada, loses a match the narrator calls maybe MAW's best ever to Steven Parker's Future Shock, beats Aaron Andrews with the Champagne Sunrise at All Or Nothing in February and loses the number one contender's final to Stevie Grayson at March Madness.

name: Aaron Andrews
caption: "Double A", a TCW star signed in February 2010 to replace Steven Parker, who loses to Champagne Lover in the contender's tournament, draws with Jay Chord for the Heavyweight title at April Showers (Rip Chord then rings the bell on his skull) and wins the Traditional title from Hugh de Aske with the Flying Body Press at Spring Fever, keeping it against Antonio in May 2010. He keeps the Traditional title in a triangle match against Casey Valentine and Jared Johnson at Summer Showdown in June 2010, against Firebird at Hotter Than Hot and against Toxin at Beach Blast, loses it to Primus Allen at Iron and to Firebird at Back To School, and with Brandon Smith beats Jay Chord and Firebird at Fall Of The King, after which the Board of Directors overrules Rip and orders his Heavyweight title match. He beats Hugh de Aske in a steel-cage match at All The Leaves Are Brown, wins the Heavyweight title from Jay Chord in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2010, by two falls to one, and keeps it against Joey Poison at Eleventh Hour in November. He keeps the Heavyweight title against Hugh de Aske at Remember November in November 2010 and Matthew Gauge at Season's Beatings, against Jay Chord in a street fight at New Year, Old Rivalries in January 2011 and Primus Allen at the Invitational, and signs a new deal for a full year in the face of Tommy Cornell's threat to pull him back to TCW. JD Morgan beats him in a non-title match at All Or Nothing in February and he is beaten down by Morgan, Firebird, Evil Spirit and Thrash until Darryl Devine drives them off; he beats Firebird at March Madness and JD Morgan at April Showers, and at the end of that match looks first at Rip Chord and then at Morgan. He and Kirk Jameson beat Firebird and Black Eagle at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 and he keeps the Heavyweight title against Black Eagle and Erik Strong in May. At High Noon on 12th June he wins the six-man Gold Rush by turning on his friend, dropping Jameson with a Standing Hot Shot onto an exposed steel turnbuckle bolt; at Summer Showdown he does it again, reopening the wound, and from then on he is the company's villain, who tells the Hotter Than Hot crowd that he will fight anyone but Jameson. He beats Fumihiro Ota, Hugh de Aske, Steve Flash, Chance Fortune and Ernest Youngman with the Flying Bodypress or the Twisting Face Crusher through September. In the diary's pages from September 2011 he keeps the Heavyweight title against Brandon Smith at Fall Of The King on 26th September, draws with Randy Bumfhole at All The Leaves Are Brown, and at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October beats Kirk Jameson, who cashes in the Invitational champion's title shot, telling him that he turned on him because he thought Jameson wanted his spot. He hires Shady K and Knuckles as Lockdown, pays them to guard him, cuts up Citizen X's shoes and is dressed down by the narrator, writes into a new contract the right to refuse any challenger, and beats Chance Fortune, Steve Flash and Fumihiro Ota. The narrator's January note says he is living up to his growing reputation as Jay Chord's successor by pranking Kirk Jameson. After Lockdown are fired at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012 he beats Randy Bumfhole in the main event, his biggest victory to date. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he keeps the Heavyweight title against Jared Johnson (the pair have zero chemistry, the narrator says), Kashmir Singh, Wanda Fish in her last match, Brandon Smith and Jim Force, has Randy Bumfhole thrown out of the Gold Rush match at April Showers on 5th April, in which he comes through without being pinned, and keeps the belt against Steve Gumble, Randy Bumfhole in a steel cage match on 12th April, his thirtieth defence, and Donnie J. At May The Force Be With You on 5th May he beats Donnie J in a title-versus-title match for the All Action belt as well, loses it back to him four days later at Great Lakes Madness, and beats him at Mother, May I? on 12th May in a thirty-minute Iron Man match by two falls to one. The narrator chews him out twice, once for being a dick backstage to Antonio and again for spreading a rumour about Jared Johnson. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he keeps the Heavyweight title against Lassana Makutsi at High Noon on 5th June, which he chooses to open the show, Fumihiro Ota at South East Madness on 9th June, in what the narrator counts as his thirty-fourth defence, KC Glenn at Summer Showdown on 12th June, Bradford Peverell at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, in what the narrator calls the worst main event in years, Kid Toma on 12th July and Rich Money in a thirty-minute draw on 5th August. The narrator fines him for spreading more rumours. At Summer Showdown he swings the belt into Kirk Jameson's head and shakes Father Johan's hand to join The Fallen; at Iron on 12th August he and The Great Ota lose to Money and Jameson, Money pinning him with the Bank Roll, and at Back To School on 5th September he tells The Fallen that the group does not work without him as champion and loses a non-title steel cage match to Money.

name: Ryan Powell
caption: A talented, fast and technically sound young Canadian whom Jean Cattley introduces as a new member of The Firm at March Madness in March 2010; he wins the first MAW Trios titles with Cattley and Darryl Devine, finishes with the Canadian Lariat and loses to Kashmir Singh's Bombay Duck at Spring Fever. He scores The Firm's second pin with the Canadian Lariat at Summer Showdown in June 2010 and is on the losing side when the Trios titles go to Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh at Hotter Than Hot in July; the narrator says he is on his way to SWF via RIPW, and SWF call him up after two weeks there.
