name: Jared Johnson
caption: An indy standout from North Carolina, a technical whiz, who turns out at April Showers in April 2010 to be Casey Valentine's partner after Cameron Vessey's departure; as Valentine & Johnson they keep the MAW Tag Team titles against Morgan & Benning and Antonio & Raphael, against Morgan & Benning again and against Shaffer & Grayson at Mother, May I?. With Casey Valentine he keeps the Tag Team titles against the Internet Favourites at Beach Blast in July 2010, Morgan & Benning at Iron and in a three-way at Back To School, carries Fall Of The King's three-way for the champions and loses the belts to the Canadian Blondes; at Where It All Begins Again in October he leaves The Firm and the partnership, saying he wants a partner who does not always have one eye on the next big score, and at Eleventh Hour in November he brings in Roderick Remus and Nelson Callum as trial partners in a Trios title match, losing in two falls. He loses Traditional title challenges on the December 2010 tour shows, then at Season's Beatings forms The Triple Threat with Roderick Remus and Nelson Callum and wins the Trios titles with the Carolina Crossface. He loses a run of tour matches to Kid Arachnid and Kashmir Singh and wins others over Amazing Fire Fly, Kashmir Singh, Matt Hocking and Ernest Youngman; at High Noon on 12th June he loses to Fumihiro Ota in a match the narrator takes as a sign of good things to come for him, and the notes keep calling him awesome, once warning that he was used too much. In the diary's pages from September 2011 he loses to Steve Flash at All The Leaves Are Brown and to Zimmy Bumfhole at Where It All Begins Again, beats Ernest Youngman at Eleventh Hour and Amazing Fire Fly at Remember November, beats Kirk Jameson with the Carolina Crossface at Season's Beatings and then fights Lockdown off to help him, draws fifteen minutes with Primus Allen for the Traditional title at End Of Days, and on 5th January 2012 teams with Wanda Fish to beat the Second Sons. He loses to Kid Arachnid in the first round of The Rip Chord Invitational; the narrator names him as one of his two projects for the coming months. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he loses to Aaron Andrews for the Heavyweight title at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, to Ford & Speed with Amazing Fire Fly, to Providence at Great Lakes Crisis and to Lord Geoffrey Windameer at April Showers, wins with KC Glenn against the Canadian Blondes at Third Time's The Charm, loses to JD Morgan at May The Force Be With You in what the narrator calls a last throw of the dice, and loses to Eddie Powell at Mother, May I? on 12th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he wins the High Noon six-man on 5th June with Thea Davis and Bradford Peverell, and as half of Team Honor with Lassana Makutsi loses to Always Breakin' Hollywood and the Second Sons, is beaten by Providence's Eye Of Providence at Great Lakes Grand Parade, and with Randy Bumfhole wins the six-man at South East Grand Parade with an MDK Powerbomb. At Iron on 12th August the same move on Casey Valentine wins Team Honor the three-way, and at Back To School on 5th September it leaves Black Eagle open to the Carolina Crossface for the Tag Team titles.

name: Amazing Fire Fly
caption: A gangly Mexican lightweight in yellow and orange gear and mask, making his pro debut at Spring Fever in April 2010 as the Chord family's chosen challenger for the Heavyweight title; Jay Chord beats him with the Cradle Piledriver, and he is on the card for Summer Showdown. He is on the losing side of the Trios title match at Summer Showdown in June 2010, loses to Jefferson Stardust at Hotter Than Hot, to Firebird at Beach Blast, to Toxin at All The Leaves Are Brown in his best match to date, and with the Internet Favourites in a trios match at Where It All Begins Again, and is brutalised by Evil Spirit in the new masked worker's debut at Eleventh Hour in November 2010. He takes his first MAW win on the 4th December 2010 tour show, loses with the Internet Favourites at End Of Days, loses to Hugh de Aske in the 2011 qualifiers and beats Antonio with the Sky High Fire Fly at April Showers; the narrator notes in March that he has won the WAM TV title in Mexico. He beats Curtis Jenkins on 25th April, loses to Jared Johnson on 4th and 11th June, and with Kid Arachnid loses a Tag Team title challenge to the Canadian Blondes at High Noon, where the match is an experiment with "twinned masks"; he beats Jefferson Stardust, Simon Ice, Extreme Deluxe and Xavier Reckless on later tour shows and loses to Curtis Jenkins and Simon Ice. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he loses to Providence at Leap Into The Unknown, with Jared Johnson to Ford & Speed at All Or Nothing and to Raphael at Spring Fever, beats Primus Allen with a Sky High Fire Fly at South East Crisis on 8th April and is attacked afterwards by Lenny Brown, and with Fumihiro Ota loses to Allen and Brown at May The Force Be With You on 5th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he loses to JD Morgan at Summer Showdown on 12th June, to Eddie Powell's Motion Censor at Hotter Than Hot, to The Great Ota at Beach Blast, where he says it sickens him to see Ota with The Fallen, and to Lord Geoffrey Windameer at Iron on 12th August, after which he hits Black Eagle with a Cutter through a table for a two count that Firebird breaks up; he is in the Back To School six-man with Donnie J and Morgan. The narrator says he cannot let him go but that his hopes for a MAW star have gone, and that he has won a second Television title in WAM.

name: Jesse Christian
caption: A veteran, "despite his advancing years", who contacts Rip about a comeback in April 2010; he works April Showers as Kashmir Singh's partner, objects to being booked to lose, and beats Findlay O'Farraday with the Torture Rack at Spring Fever. He beats Primus Allen at Beach Blast in July 2010 when Findlay O'Farraday's boot misfires, beats Nelson Callum with the Human Torture Rack at Iron in August, and leaves the company after Where It All Begins Again in October 2010, the narrator noting that "the guy complained about losing too much".

name: Ricochet
caption: One of three masked newcomers who ambush Fumihiro Ota, "Bulldozer" Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh in the boiler room at Mother, May I? in May 2010; he debuts that night against Singh and wins with a Cross Armbreaker, and is on the card for Summer Showdown with Sharp. He loses to Brandon Smith at Summer Showdown in June 2010, beats Fumihiro Ota with the Cross Armbreaker in a twenty-minute match at Fall Of The King in September, and forces the Masked Patriot to submit in a three-way at Where It All Begins Again in October. At Eleventh Hour in November Firebird has him unmask as Marc Speed, "a man who lived life as though it would last forever". As Marc Speed, one half of Ford & Speed, he beats the Bailey Boys at Remember November in November 2010, loses a qualifier to Steve Flash at Season's Beatings and loses to Morgan & Benning at End Of Days; the team beat the Young Americans at April Showers. As Marc Speed he and Greg Ford tell the crowd on 12th May 2011 that they are no longer associated with The Fallen but still follow its ideals and will claim the Tag Team titles; he forces Stevie Grayson to tap to a Cross Armbar that night and beats Singh & Smith with a Cross Armbreaker at Summernova. As Ford & Speed he beats Amazing Fire Fly and Jared Johnson at All Or Nothing and the West Texas Peacekeepers at March Madness, and loses a singles match to Brandon Smith's Inverted Piledriver at Mother, May I? on 12th May. As Ford & Speed in the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he beats KC Glenn and Bradford Peverell at South East Madness on 9th June and the West Texas Peacekeepers at Summernova on 5th August, and Smith & Singh at Back To School on 5th September, all with Fallen Chances, and loses the High Noon three-way on 5th June.

name: Sharp
caption: The silver-clad one of three masked newcomers who attack Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh at Mother, May I? in May 2010; he loses to Smith's Backdrop Driver in his first match and is on the card for Summer Showdown with Ricochet. He loses to Kashmir Singh's Bombay Duck at Fall Of The King in September 2010 and again in a rematch at Where It All Begins Again in October. At Eleventh Hour in November Firebird has him unmask as Greg Ford, known to some as Sammy The Shark, a gambler who "gambled everything, and won". As Greg Ford, one half of Ford & Speed, he loses a qualifier to the Masked Patriot at Season's Beatings in December 2010; he beats Matt Hocking in February 2011 and Kashmir Singh in March, loses to Brandon Smith and leaves NYCW. As Greg Ford he beats Brandon Smith on 4th May and Amazing Fire Fly on 11th May, loses to Kid Arachnid on 25th April, and takes part in Ford & Speed's wins over Stevie Grayson and Thomas Morgan, Smith & Singh and the West Texas Peacekeepers. As Ford & Speed he pins Amazing Fire Fly with Fallen Chances at All Or Nothing and beats the West Texas Peacekeepers at March Madness, and loses to Kashmir Singh at Great Lakes Madness. As Ford & Speed in the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he and Ricochet lose the three-way at High Noon on 5th June and beat KC Glenn and Bradford Peverell at South East Madness on 9th June, the West Texas Peacekeepers at Summernova on 5th August and Smith & Singh at Back To School on 5th September, the narrator calling them talented workers who rarely drop out of the D range.

name: Toxin
caption: The third of the masked newcomers who attack Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh at Mother, May I? in May 2010; he beats Ota with a roll-up in his first match. He loses a Traditional title match to Aaron Andrews at Beach Blast in July 2010, beats Fumihiro Ota with a tight cradle at Where It All Begins Again in October and Amazing Fire Fly with the same cradle at All The Leaves Are Brown, loses to Steve Flash at Fall Of The King, and at Eleventh Hour in November unmasks as Joey Poison and loses a Heavyweight title challenge to Aaron Andrews. He loses to Jean Cattley in a qualifier at Remember November in November 2010 and to Kirk Jameson at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011, and leaves MAW after nine months when he asks for $1,500 an appearance.

name: Masked Patriot #21
caption: A fan in a stars-and-stripes mask, with a sign calling himself Masked Patriot #21, who is photographed with the Patriot at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2010; the Patriot takes him under his wing, and when Brandon Smith unmasks at March Madness in March 2010 he becomes the new Masked Patriot in The Watch, loses to Primus Allen's Running Powerslam at Spring Fever and beats Raphael with a Patriot Slam at Mother, May I?. He takes Jay Chord close in a Heavyweight title challenge at Beach Blast in July 2010, with the Delaware crowd calling Jay a Commie, loses to Hugh de Aske at Summernova and to Jean Cattley at Back To School, and is the target of Jay's jibes about his mask and tights until Rip warns Jay off. He is forced to submit to Ricochet in a three-way with Kirk Jameson at Where It All Begins Again in October, and the narrator's roster overview calls him the "protégé" of Brandon Smith whom the game's auto-push put above his teacher. He beats Firebird with the Patriot Slam at Remember November in November 2010, beats Greg Ford at Season's Beatings and loses to Primus Allen at New Year, Old Rivalries and Hugh de Aske in the 2011 Invitational. Firebird's taunts make him hesitant, and he loses to Firebird in February, is thrown by Thrash with Fumihiro Ota at All Or Nothing, and at March Madness beats Thrash and refuses Firebird's offered hand. He loses to JD Morgan's Cross Atlantic Stretch at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, spears Thrash and chairs Hugh de Aske on 12th May, and at Mother, May I? on 26th May appears in a new black-and-red mask, re-christened Providence by Firebird, saying "I am Providence", and loses the Traditional title match to Hugh de Aske before bowing low to him. Sienna LeNoir comes with him, and he pins Max Mayhem with JD Morgan at Hotter Than Hot, beats Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson with Firebird at Summer Showdown, beats Bradford Peverell with the Eye Of Providence at Summernova, and loses to Kirk Jameson when Jameson drives his skull into the exposed steel at Back To School. As Providence he beats Brandon Smith at All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October 2011 and Fumihiro Ota at Where It All Begins Again, beats Kirk Jameson and Kid Arachnid with Citizen X at Remember November, loses an All Action three-way to JD Morgan at End Of Days and loses a first-round Invitational tie to Fumihiro Ota on 12th January 2012; the narrator's note of 1st November calls him a personal project, an unhinged character he enjoys writing for. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 as Providence he beats Amazing Fire Fly at Leap Into The Unknown, loses to Brandon Smith at All Or Nothing, beats Jared Johnson at Great Lakes Crisis, Lassana Makutsi at Third Time's The Charm and Steve Gumble at Mother, May I? on 12th May, and loses to Kirk Jameson at April Showers; he tells Jameson that he lives by impulse and that his warning to stay out of his business is the last, and at Mother, May I? tells the crowd that everyone will get what is coming to them, "We'll make sure of that". In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 as Providence he turns up with a clown face painted on at Summer Showdown on 12th June, draws with Kirk Jameson and spears KC Glenn, and stands over the beaten faces with the rest of The Fallen when Aaron Andrews turns on them; he beats Thea Davis and Jaime Quine with Father Johan at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, Jared Johnson at Great Lakes Grand Parade, loses with The Great Ota to Jameson and JD Morgan at Summernova, loses a ladder match for the All Action title to Donnie J at South East Grand Parade, and wins the Back To School six-man with Eddie Powell and Sean Deeley. TEW.com, the narrator's news says, again calls him a star of the future, able to play heel and face roles and a wide variety of characters.

name: TJ Bailey
caption: A flyweight, one half of The Bailey Boys, who makes his on-screen debut with CB Bailey at Summer Showdown in June 2010, where the pair beat Primus Allen and Findlay O'Farraday. He brings some brawling to a Summernova match with the Canadian Blondes in August, falls to Jefferson Stardust's Encore Extraordinaire at Back To School in September, and takes risks in the four-team ladder match for the Tag Team titles at Where It All Begins Again in October 2010. The narrator's roster overview calls the Baileys "lightweight jobbers to whom I throw the occasional bone" who "bump pretty well". He is caught in a Cross Armbreaker by Marc Speed at Remember November in November 2010 and leaves MAW in February 2011 with his contract expired.

name: CB Bailey
caption: CB ("Cheetah Boy") Bailey, the other Bailey Boy, who comes off the top rope to pin Findlay O'Farraday and score the upset over Primus Allen and Findlay at the team's on-screen debut at Summer Showdown in June 2010. He pins Jefferson Stardust with a Flying Pounce at All The Leaves Are Brown in October 2010 and is in the ladder match for the Tag Team titles at Where It All Begins Again later that month. He is caught in a Canadian Crab by Flash Savage at Season's Beatings in December 2010 and leaves MAW in February 2011 with his contract expired.

name: Evil Spirit
caption: A spooky-looking Japanese worker in a heavily stylised mask bearing a demon's face, leather ring gear and a heavy greatcoat, who debuts at Eleventh Hour in November 2010 to haunting Japanese music with a brutal win over Amazing Fire Fly and keeps beating Fly down after the bell. Firebird names him as Fumihiro Ota's former student, abandoned by Ota for seeking the darkness, and as the means by which he will bring Ota into the dark; he beats Matt Hocking on the 25th November tour show. He is Firebird's partner at Season's Beatings in December 2010, beating the Internet Favourites, loses tour matches to Hugh Lee and Riley McManus, beats Jonnie Perez in February 2011, beats Fumihiro Ota and the Masked Patriot with Firebird at All Or Nothing and is put on his last warning for spreading rumours about Jay Chord, then loses to his former master Ota at Third Time's The Charm. Firebird names him at Mother, May I? on 26th May 2011 as a man who has "gone from this place" to serve as an example; the narrator lists him among the June departures, saying that he put a lot of effort into Spirit and it never clicked.

name: Steve Flash
caption: A veteran past forty-five, whom the narrator introduces at Back To School in September 2010 as the challenger the Board of Directors has chosen for Jay Chord; he schools the champion for a quarter of an hour before Jay's Cradle Piledriver beats him. He beats Toxin with the Flash Bang at Fall Of The King, reverses Hugh de Aske's Cutthroat Driver into a Flash Bang at Where It All Begins Again in October, and goes to a time-limit draw with Primus Allen at Eleventh Hour in November. The narrator's roster overview says he will use Flash as "awesome, get little or no mic time, and be worshipped by everyone". He beats Marc Speed in a qualifier at Season's Beatings in December 2010, teams with Aaron Andrews against Jay Chord and Primus Allen at End Of Days and loses, and loses a quarter-final to Firebird at the Invitational on 21st January 2011. He beats Robert Thomas at Third Time's The Charm and loses to Jay Chord at March Madness. The narrator wants to do more with him than good matches. He beats Thrash at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 and, asked by Jean Cattley to keep The Firm's legacy going, gathers Chance Fortune, Randy Bumfhole and, as the fourth man, Kid Arachnid in the old Firm's dressing room to take on the Second Sons and The Fallen. He loses with Arachnid to Erik Strong and Jay Chord on 12th May and to JD Morgan at Mother, May I? in the narrator's B-, beats Casey Valentine at High Noon and Summer Showdown and Antonio at Hotter Than Hot, wins with Randy Bumfhole at Beach Blast and introduces his "nephew" Ernest Youngman. At 45 he loses a Heavyweight title challenge to Aaron Andrews at Summernova and a three-way for the Traditional title at Back To School, and with Fortune and Bumfhole promises to be the narrator's ears and eyes in the locker room. He beats Jared Johnson at All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October 2011 and Roderick Remus at Where It All Begins Again, and loses to Aaron Andrews's sleeper hold for the Heavyweight title at Remember November on 26th November; the same night he tells the narrator that, at forty-five and a grandfather, he is leaving for the SWF for the money.

name: Jonnie Perez
caption: A hot young prospect billed as the brother of Frankie Perez, one of three newcomers the narrator brings in after Beach Blast in July 2010. He and Kirk Jameson lose to Roderick Remus and Jean Cattley at Summernova, he loses a poor opener to Remus at All The Leaves Are Brown, and at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2010 taps out Primus Allen to the P-Clutch in his third MAW match to win the Traditional title, which he keeps against Raphael, Curtis Jenkins and Antonio on the November tour shows. He keeps the Traditional title against Jared Johnson, Roderick Remus, Matthew Gauge and Jefferson Stardust in December 2010 and January 2011 and loses it to Gauge at the Invitational on 21st January; he loses the three-way at Leap Into The Unknown, loses to Hugh de Aske in February and to Black Eagle at April Showers. He beats Nelson Callum on 11th and 25th May, Extreme Deluxe on 4th July and Oscar Golden on 25th September, loses to Raphael and VIP Wallace and is squashed by Primus Allen at Beach Blast. In the diary's pages for August 2012 the narrator reports that he left the company when his contract expired, calling him the reason for MAW's existence as a way of seasoning future stars, though he had no improvement in him, and noting that he had ten defences of the Traditional title.

name: Roderick Remus
caption: A project the narrator brings in after Beach Blast in July 2010: his brother's motorbike accident in 2006 put the brother into retirement and left Rod on his own, and he had not had his head in the game since. He teams with Jean Cattley to beat Jonnie Perez and Kirk Jameson at Summernova, beats Perez with the Remus Clutch in the awful opener of All The Leaves Are Brown, and is one of Jared Johnson's trial partners in the Trios title match at Eleventh Hour in November 2010. He is still rusty in December 2010 and joins Jared Johnson and Nelson Callum as The Triple Threat at Season's Beatings, winning the Trios titles. He keeps the Trios titles with The Triple Threat until Summernova on 12th August 2011; on the tour shows he beats Max Mayhem and Matt Hocking and loses to Kashmir Singh and Kid Arachnid and, as Rod Remus, with Nelson Callum to the Internet Favourites. In the diary's pages for August 2012 the narrator reports that he left when his contract expired, ending the attempts to make silk purses from sows' ears; of his Trios partners Nelson Callum is also gone and Jared Johnson still works for MAW.

name: Nelson Callum
caption: A newcomer "working for beans" who comes to MAW after a miserable time in PSW. He debuts at Iron in August 2010 and loses to Jesse Christian's Human Torture Rack, joins Glamour And Devastation in a trios match at Where It All Begins Again in October, evening the match with an Ankle Lock on Hugh Lee, and is one of Jared Johnson's trial partners at Eleventh Hour in November. He wins a tour match over Amazing Fire Fly in December 2010 and joins Jared Johnson and Roderick Remus as The Triple Threat at Season's Beatings, winning the Trios titles. He keeps the Trios titles with The Triple Threat until Summernova on 12th August 2011, when Kid Arachnid pins him with the Cradle Piledriver; the narrator, who has booked Arachnid against Callum three times, wants "Arachnid + Callum = bad" tattooed on his forehead. He loses tour matches to Jonnie Perez, Kid Arachnid and Joe Benning. In the diary's pages from February 2012 the narrator is shown him through a cell hatch after an arrest for possession of illegal narcotics; he tells the press MAW has a zero-tolerance policy on performance-enhancing drugs and releases Callum from his contract with immediate effect. Callum and his lawyer arrive at MAW HQ muttering about unfair dismissal until Rip Chord goes ballistic, and the narrator blames him for the loss of the company's prestige.

name: Matt Hocking
caption: An import from FCW whom the narrator's roster overview calls "painfully average in all categories": he wears sunglasses, and uses a Dude gimmick because he has long hair and glasses. He loses to Casey Valentine on the 11th November 2010 tour show, to Evil Spirit on the 25th, and is booked against "Lone Wolf" Robert Thomas in a Rip Chord Invitational qualifier on the card for Remember November. He loses to Robert Thomas in a qualifier at Remember November in November 2010 and is named as a possible cut in January 2011; in April 2011 he and Joe Benning are billed as The Young Americans. He is on the losing side of the Young Americans' matches against the Canadian Blondes, The Triple Threat, the West Texas Peacekeepers, Valentine and Antonio and, with Ota, the Second Sons; on the tours he loses to Jefferson Stardust, Roderick Remus and Jared Johnson.

name: Robert Thomas
caption: "Lone Wolf" Robert Thomas, called Bobby Thomas by the narrator, who "has arrived" in MAW in October 2010: too expensive for the touring shows, short of the star quality to crack the top of the card, he plays a brooding loner and squabbles with Fumihiro Ota over who gets to use the boiler room. He is a debutant on the card for Remember November, against Matt Hocking in a Rip Chord Invitational qualifier. He wins a qualifier over Matt Hocking at Remember November in November 2010, but a booking in CGC takes him out of the Invitational itself and his quarter-final is played as a bonus match on the 18th January 2011 tour show, which Jean Cattley wins; his matches at Leap Into The Unknown and Third Time's The Charm are marred by bad chemistry, and the narrator thinks his loss to Kirk Jameson at April Showers is the first to get the best out of him. On 26th May 2011 he loses to Chance Fortune in an extended tryout that the narrator calls his first decent match, is listed among the expendables for lack of direction and low match quality, and after his dark matches at High Noon is added to the release list with Findlay O'Farraday; he leaves in June.

name: Bret Graveson
caption: A MAW referee, who warns Jay Chord over a low blow in the thirty-minute Iron Man match with Aaron Andrews at Where It All Begins Again in October 2010, counts the pinfalls and, after the bell, learns that Jay's shoulders were down for the full three count while Andrews raised his at two, and hands the Heavyweight title to Andrews. The November tour notes record a prank of his on Flash Savage that backfires and a warning to him about passing rumours about Jared Johnson. He is the referee who calls for the bell at New Year, Old Rivalries and All Or Nothing, is repeatedly fined or warned for pranks on the tour shows, and is dismissed in March 2011 in one of the quickest meetings the narrator has held.

name: VIP Wallace
caption: A newcomer, also called Air Attack Weasel, whose MAW career starts flat at All Or Nothing in February 2011, when he beats Stevie Grayson, whose contract the narrator and Rip Chord have agreed not to renew, in a match that scores D-. The narrator then keeps him winning to burn off ring rust: Amazing Fire Fly on the 4th March tour show, Jonnie Perez on the 11th, Hugh Lee on the 18th and Thom Morgan with the Air Attack Ace at March Madness, where the narrator says he will give him promo time "any day now". He loses with Raphael to the Internet Favourites on 4th April and teams without chemistry with Casey Valentine on the 11th, then loses to Brandon Smith on the 18th in a match the tour notes call excellent in chemistry. He loses to Kid Arachnid on 4th May, beats Jonnie Perez on 25th June and Riley McManus on 18th July, loses to and beats Hugh Lee, wins with Jefferson Stardust over the West Texas Peacekeepers and The Quest on 18th August and loses to Ernest Youngman on 11th September; the narrator lists him among the expendables for lack of direction. He beats Hugh Lee, and Matt Hocking and Nelson Callum together, on the October 2011 tour shows and is released with ten others on 1st November, annoyed at being counted among the dregs of the roster.

name: Thrash
caption: A monstrous man in black leather who vaults the barrier at All Or Nothing on 26th February 2011 to throw Fumihiro Ota and the Masked Patriot around after their loss to Firebird and Evil Spirit; Firebird presents him as one who "embraced the darkness from birth" and has now been shown the light, and he joins The Fallen. He joins the four-on-one beating of Aaron Andrews after JD Morgan's win, beats Andrews and Kirk Jameson with JD Morgan at Third Time's The Charm with the Grease Spot, loses to the Masked Patriot's Patriot Slam at March Madness and, with Firebird, loses a Tag Team title challenge to Cattley and Singh at April Showers when Firebird declines to help him. The narrator's out-of-character note names the game wrestler behind the debut as Grease Hogg. He loses to Steve Flash in a short match at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, the narrator's "designated Fallen fall taker", and to the Masked Patriot's spear into the crowd barrier on 12th May; at Mother, May I? Firebird names him with Evil Spirit and Toxin as men who have "gone from this place" to serve as an example.

The diary's own out-of-character note (p310) says the debut is of "Thrash (Grease Hogg, for those wondering)": the canon figure behind the stage name, so the stage name is a character of this diary and the canon name an aka.

name: JD Morgan
caption: A veteran with a technical, old-school style whom Rip Chord produces at All Or Nothing on 26th February 2011 as a challenger for Aaron Andrews: he dominates Andrews in a non-title match and beats him with A Shot Of JD, then joins Firebird, Evil Spirit and Thrash in a four-on-one beating of the champion that Darryl Devine breaks up with a chair. He and Thrash beat Andrews and Kirk Jameson at Third Time's The Charm, he goes to a time-limit draw with Jameson at March Madness, and at April Showers he loses to Andrews in a twenty-five-minute match that ends with Andrews's Rip Chord DDT. The narrator calls him The Fallen's most recent high-profile signing, and Firebird counts him among his followers. He beats the Masked Patriot with the Cross Atlantic Stretch at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, Chance Fortune on 12th May and Steve Flash with A Shot Of JD at Mother, May I? (the narrator's B-). He is Firebird's silent enforcer; at High Noon he eliminates Hugh de Aske and is knocked out on the exposed steel bolt by Aaron Andrews, loses to Fumihiro Ota at Summer Showdown, beats the Internet Favourites with Providence at Hotter Than Hot, loses to Jay Chord at Beach Blast and to Kirk Jameson at Iron, where Firebird watches over him. The narrator calls him third or fourth in his group and thinks he may have a future outside it. In the diary's pages from September 2011 he beats Hugh de Aske at Fall Of The King, Bradford Peverell at All The Leaves Are Brown and Ernest Youngman at Where It All Begins Again, helps Firebird to ambush Kirk Jameson, and wins the ten-man battle royal at Eleventh Hour on 12th November for his first MAW title, the All Action title, for which he is required to defend in randomly chosen matches; he loses it on the night of Remember November, regains it, and from End Of Days on 26th December has Haley Buck as his manager. He keeps it against Jonnie Perez and Providence, beats Riley McManus on 5th January 2012, Wanda Fish and Fumihiro Ota in The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January and loses the final to Kid Arachnid. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he keeps the All Action title against Bradford Peverell, Wanda Fish and Fumihiro Ota in a Triple Threat, Kashmir Singh and Kirk Jameson in a submission match, with Haley Buck at his side, wins the Gold Rush match at April Showers on 5th April, taking the Traditional title from Primus Allen, loses the All Action belt to Donnie J in a ladder match at South East Crisis on 8th April, beats Jared Johnson at May The Force Be With You and keeps the Traditional title against Bradford Peverell and Lord Geoffrey Windameer at Mother, May I? on 12th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he keeps the Traditional title against Steve Gumble in a draw at High Noon on 5th June, Amazing Fire Fly at Summer Showdown on 12th June, Gumble at Hotter Than Hot, Donnie J in a draw at Great Lakes Grand Parade, Black Eagle at Beach Blast, Sean Deeley at South East Grand Parade and Rudy Velasquez at Iron on 12th August. He turns down The Fallen's invitation to join, telling Father Johan he stands alone and Haley Buck that he will not pitch his tent on a viper's nest, hits Father Johan with an elbow at Great Lakes Grand Parade and agrees to help Donnie J and KC Glenn when he is in trouble, without joining the Knights Templar; Haley Buck takes on Deeley instead. At Summernova on 5th August he and Kirk Jameson beat Providence and The Great Ota, and at Back To School on 5th September Deeley pins him in a six-man match.

name: Pee-Wee Germaine
caption: A referee from CZCW whom the narrator contacts in March 2011 to work MAW's shows after the dismissal of Bret Graveson; the narrator says he is not as good a referee as Bret "but he's more reliable".

name: Tommy Cornell
caption: The head of TCW, who telephones the narrator after the street fight at New Year, Old Rivalries in January 2011, furious that Aaron Andrews was "mangled" in what he calls a rip-off of DaVE, and says he is pulling Andrews out of MAW; the narrator reminds him of their agreement and says that Andrews and Jay Chord both signed new deals before the show, Andrews for a full year. The narrator later says that Tommy's orders made Darryl Devine balk at losing to Jay, and that Tommy has put the two men together as a team out west, possibly out of spite. In mid-September 2011 he telephones the narrator, complains of Jay Chord's mouth and offers him the job of TCW's head road agent, with relocation costs and a place for Katie Cameron, saying that TCW is a few months from going global and that it is "harvest time for Rip Chord"; earlier, TCW's A* show opposite the 11th May tour show has Tommy in a match with Wolf Hawkins.

name: Richard Eisen
caption: The owner of the SWF, who finds the narrator after the touring show in Ohio on 4th March 2011, takes him to dinner and offers him the job of head booker; the narrator tells him that he would need complete control of hirings and firings and a company "unrecognisable" in six months, and the offer is withdrawn. The narrator reports the offer to Rip Chord the next day and Rip asks whether he would have taken it. In the diary's pages for July 2012 the narrator tells Rip Chord that he is going to break him in two, and Rip agrees on condition that MAW does not define itself by Eisen.

name: Yusuke Takahama
caption: A worker on the touring shows, who loses a four-team match to the Internet Favourites with Zeshin Makioka on the 4th January 2011 Great Lakes show and a triple threat to Makioka on the 18th February show. He leaves MAW in June 2011 as one of Evil Spirit's locker-room companions.

name: Zeshin Makioka
caption: A worker on the touring shows, who loses a four-team match to the Internet Favourites with Yusuke Takahama on the 4th January 2011 Great Lakes show and, the diary's results line spelling his name Makloka, wins a triple threat over Takahama and Ultimo Soetsu on 18th February. He leaves MAW in June 2011 as one of Evil Spirit's locker-room companions.

name: Ultimo Soetsu
caption: A worker on the touring shows, who loses a four-team match with Evil Spirit on the 4th January 2011 Great Lakes show and a triple threat to Zeshin Makioka on 18th February. He leaves MAW in June 2011 as one of Evil Spirit's locker-room companions.

name: Chance Fortune
caption: A veteran whom the commentary introduces as a former TCW star and who walks out with Randy Bumfhole at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 to face Erik Strong and Antonio, the match ending on a Bumfhole Buster. He joins Steve Flash's new Firm, loses to JD Morgan on 12th May, beats "Lone Wolf" Robert Thomas with the Stroke of Luck on 26th May, loses to Erik Strong at High Noon, is ambushed backstage and beaten by Primus Allen at Summer Showdown, and beats Black Eagle at Beach Blast. With Kid Arachnid and Bumfhole he wins the Trios titles from The Triple Threat at Summernova on 12th August, and at Iron on 26th August takes his first Heavyweight title shot in the company and loses to Aaron Andrews. At the narrator's request he is one of the three veterans, with Flash and Bumfhole, who agree to be his ears and eyes in the locker room. At All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October 2011 he brings Zimmy Bumfhole to The Firm's rescue; at Where It All Begins Again The Firm lose the Trios titles to the Second Sons, and at Farewell Tour on 22nd November he loses a Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews; the narrator then thanks him as he and Ernest Youngman and Hugh de Aske drive north to the SWF.

name: Randy Bumfhole
caption: A former SWF worker, dropped by Richard Eisen shortly before Spring Fever, who debuts there with Chance Fortune on 23rd April 2011 and whom the narrator calls possibly the most talented worker on the roster; his pay of $3,000 a show is the figure the rest of the roster will want matched. He joins Steve Flash's new Firm, beats Casey Valentine on 12th May, loses with Kid Arachnid to Valentine and Antonio on 26th May, is ambushed and held to a time-limit draw by Antonio at High Noon, beats Erik Strong at Summer Showdown and Black Eagle at Hotter Than Hot and, with Flash, beats Antonio and Strong at Beach Blast. He wins the Trios titles with Arachnid and Chance Fortune at Summernova on 12th August and pins Firebird with the Bumfhole Buster in the first defence at Back To School. In August the narrator reports that he has signed with TCW. At Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 he beats Jay Chord in a twenty-five-minute match with the Bumfhole Buster, winning a Heavyweight title shot, which he cashes in at All The Leaves Are Brown for a time-limit draw with Aaron Andrews. With his brother Zimmy as The Fabulous Bumfholes he pins Andrews at Eleventh Hour on 12th November; the narrator wants him to sign for the next year, and tew.com reports Richard Eisen's plan to raid him. After the departures to the SWF he is the locker room's answer to Andrews, wins a rematch clause, beats Knuckles with Kirk Jameson and Fumihiro Ota at End Of Days and Nathan Coleman with Jameson on 5th January 2012, and loses the Heavyweight title match to Andrews at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January, cut over his left eye and with a wrecked ankle. In the diary's pages from February to April 2012 he loses to Firebird at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, beats Black Eagle with the Bumfhole Buster when he and KC Glenn beat the Dark Raptors at All Or Nothing, is beaten up backstage by Primus Allen and loses the Traditional title match to him at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March, is kicked out of the Gold Rush match by Aaron Andrews at April Showers and loses a steel cage Heavyweight title match to Andrews at Spring Fever on 12th April, injuring his knee. The narrator writes that he refused to re-sign and has left MAW: twenty-five matches at an average C for $3,000 a time. In the diary's pages from August to September 2012 he returns at South East Grand Parade on 9th August for a few shows, thanks to Rich Money and Kirk Jameson, to take revenge on Aaron Andrews, and wins the six-man there with Team Honor; the narrator's news has him signed to what appear to be the last days of 4C. At Back To School on 5th September he draws with The Great Ota, whom he calls his former friend, in a thrilling clash.

name: Ernest Youngman
caption: An eighteen-year-old from the independent scene, called the Assassin of the Squared Circle and King Midas, whom the narrator signs in August 2011 for $800 a night after talking Rip Chord into watching him; his announcement that he was going pro was on his blog. Steve Flash presents him to The Firm at Summernova on 12th August as his nephew, whom he trained himself, and he loses his debut to Erik Strong; at Iron he is fed to Primus Allen for the Traditional title in an extended squash and at Back To School he takes a Heavyweight title shot against Aaron Andrews, losing both. On the tour and Moment Of Madness shows he beats Jefferson Stardust, VIP Wallace, Curtis Jenkins, Flash Savage, Simon Ice and Raphael and loses to Jared Johnson, the notes calling the September shows "the Ernest Youngman show". He loses to Jared Johnson at Eleventh Hour, to JD Morgan at Where It All Begins Again and, in a submission match for the All Action title, at Farewell Tour on 22nd November, after which the narrator says goodbye to him as he leaves for the SWF with Chance Fortune and Hugh de Aske.
aka: The Assassin of the Squared Circle

name: Bradford Peverell
caption: A tall, rangy newcomer who rides a battered motorbike down the ramp at Summernova on 12th August 2011 to interrupt Providence, tells the crowd that where he comes from people like Providence are locked up and that he looked after his neighbourhood, and promises that people will know Bradford Peverell is a force to be reckoned with. He loses his debut to Providence's Eye Of Providence in a match the narrator scores for no chemistry; the narrator calls him The Pev. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he loses to JD Morgan for the All Action title at Leap Into The Unknown, beats Raphael with a Dream Left Hook at Third Time's The Charm and Eddie Powell at May The Force Be With You, loses to Firebird at March Madness and, at Mother, May I? on 12th May, loses a three-way for the Traditional title against JD Morgan and Lord Geoffrey Windameer. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he wins the six-man at High Noon on 5th June with Thea Davis and Jared Johnson, landing the Dream Left Hook on Raphael, loses to Father Johan's Crucifix Powerbomb at Summer Showdown on 12th June and suggests there that the four men who stand against The Fallen need a symbol. He loses a Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, in what the narrator calls the worst main event in years, and with Kirk Jameson loses to Firebird and The Great Ota at South East Grand Parade on 9th August; Jameson credits him with saying that people need a symbol to rally behind.

name: Simon Ice
caption: An English high-flyer, the first of the twelve cheap signings of June 2011, whom Rip Chord brings over for less than the plane fare; he works as a heel who acts as the future of the business, and the narrator rates his potential at 4/10. He loses on the 25th June Tri-State tour show, to Amazing Fire Fly on 18th August, to Ben Williams on 22nd August and to Ernest Youngman on 22nd September, and beats Williams and Amazing Fire Fly on 8th September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand.

name: The American Flash
caption: A moderately talented high-flyer signed in June 2011 whom the narrator describes as effectively Masked Patriot #22, an archetypal spot monkey of 3/10 potential. He loses with Leftie Wilkes to Curtis Jenkins and Smart Mark on the 18th July tour show and beats Smart Mark and Simon Ice on 1st September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand.

name: Leftie Wilkes
caption: The younger brother of Duberry Excess, with almost as daft a name, signed in June 2011 as a generic friendly face and a modern cruiserweight with a solid technical base (4/10). He loses with The American Flash on 18th July, is squashed with Ben Williams by the Canadian Blondes in six minutes for the Tag Team titles at Beach Blast on 26th July, beats Super Sonic on 22nd August (who pranks him backstage) and Curtis Jenkins on 22nd September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand.

name: Fearless Blue
caption: One of the five XDW survivors signed in June 2011 (potential 3/10), a flyer who, with Daredevil Aero, is booked to feel guilty about the past and try to stop the others. He beats Smart Mark on 22nd August and loses to Super Sonic on 8th September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand; the narrator cites his hiring as an example of Rip Chord hiring everyone and anyone.

name: Extreme Deluxe
caption: One of the five XDW survivors signed in June 2011 (potential 2/10), the leader in the storyline of the backyard and hardcore assault on MAW by Xavier Reckless and Super Sonic. He loses to Jonnie Perez on 4th July, with Super Sonic to Riley McManus and Jonnie Perez on 18th July, to Amazing Fire Fly on 1st September and to Kid Arachnid on 15th September, and beats Curtis Jenkins on 8th September; the 11th July notes say that he and Xavier Reckless have great chemistry. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand.

name: Super Sonic
caption: One of the five XDW survivors signed in June 2011 (potential 2/10), a flyer who follows Extreme Deluxe in the assault on MAW. He loses with Deluxe on 18th July, to Leftie Wilkes on 22nd August after pranking him backstage and earning a mild warning, and wins an 8th September Moment Of Madness main event over Fearless Blue and Xavier Reckless that the notes call a mistake, a heel-versus-heel match, after he spreads rumours about Simon Ice. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand; he had two disciplinary incidents that year.

name: Xavier Reckless
caption: The brawler of the five XDW survivors signed in June 2011 (potential 4/10), whom the narrator thinks the pick of the bunch and a possible manager. After the first Tri-State show the narrator reprimands him in front of the locker room for punching out a fan who called him backyard, and tells the XDW group bluntly that they do not yet have a place on the main shows; the notes later record him pranking Super Sonic and others. He loses to Super Sonic on 8th September and to Amazing Fire Fly on 22nd September. Released with ten others on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand, he takes it worst and tells Rip to take his reference and his company; the narrator records that he appeared on twelve shows and made trouble at four, and four disciplinary incidents in the year.

name: Daredevil Aero
caption: One of the five XDW survivors signed in June 2011 (potential 3/10), a flyer who, with Fearless Blue, is booked to feel guilty about the past. He is pinned by Oscar Golden with the O, Canada! when The Quest challenge the Canadian Blondes for the Tag Team titles at Iron on 26th August, and beats Jefferson Stardust on 8th September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand.

name: Ben Williams
caption: "The Bump Machine", signed in June 2011 to lose to the heels and make them look good: a consistent seller who has worked a million gimmicks on the independents and is only moderately good in his best areas (2/10). He loses to Raphael on 4th July and Jefferson Stardust on 18th July, is squashed with Leftie Wilkes by the Canadian Blondes at Beach Blast, beats Simon Ice on 22nd August and loses to Simon Ice on 8th September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand.

name: Smart Mark
caption: The Internet heel Mark Smart, signed in June 2011 as an obnoxious lightweight who criticises and hypes other workers and may make a decent manager; the narrator thinks he could fit a CZCW-style fed (5/10). He loses to Joe Benning on 11th July, wins with Curtis Jenkins over Leftie Wilkes and The American Flash on 18th July and loses to Fearless Blue on 22nd August and to The American Flash on 1st September. One of the eleven workers released on 1st November 2011 when Rip Chord ends the third brand (the narrator's list writes his name as Mark Smart).

name: Marshall Dillon
caption: Half of the West Texas Peacekeepers, a tough cowboy from Dallas signed in June 2011 after a developmental deal with RIPW that did not work out (5.5/10). He is the victim of the Canadian Blondes' O, Canada! at Summer Showdown on 26th June, is pinned by Ford & Speed's Fallen Chances at Iron and wins the 4th July and 18th July Ontario tour matches with his partner. In the diary's pages from June to August 2012 he is crushed by Lenny Brown's The Star Treatment at High Noon on 5th June, loses a Tag Team title challenge to the Dark Raptors at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, and is pinned by Ford at Summernova on 5th August with Fallen Chances.

name: Bradley Blaze
caption: Half of the West Texas Peacekeepers, an eighteen-year-old cowboy just out of training whom the narrator rates the best prospect of the June 2011 signings (7/10); the diary lists him as Bradley (Sheriff) Blaze. He and Marshall Dillon lose to the Canadian Blondes for the Tag Team titles at Summer Showdown and to Ford & Speed at Iron.

name: Jenna
caption: Rip Chord's assistant, who tells the narrator in May 2011 that she will pass messages between him and Rip behind Rip's closed door and who makes herself scarce in June while Rip interviews sixteen cheap workers.

name: Zimmy Bumfhole
caption: Randy Bumfhole's brother, whom Chance Fortune introduces at All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October 2011 as an old friend of Randy's who is "actually a member of the family". He shakes hands with Fortune and charges the ring with him, and The Firm's pair beat the Second Sons when he pins Antonio with a Bumfhole In One; afterwards he and Fortune are jumped by Cameron Vessey with a kendo stick. He beats Jared Johnson at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October in a match the narrator scores D-, and says he has come for a few weeks to help his brother. At Eleventh Hour on 12th November, his last night with the company for a while, he and Randy come out together as The Fabulous Bumfholes, the first time in over a year in America, and beat Aaron Andrews and Primus Allen when Randy pins the champion; the narrator says he was not booked to be squashed on his way out, though he bumped hardest for Allen.

name: Shady K
caption: One half of the former SWF team the tew.com notes call Death Row, a rising pair; Aaron Andrews buys them as "insurance" and introduces them at Eleventh Hour on 12th November 2011 as Lockdown, men who care only for cold hard cash. He crushes Hugh Lee with a K Killer that night, beats Team OMGsplosion with the K Krusher at Farewell Tour on 22nd November, and puts Marshall Dillon away with the K Killer at Remember November. With Knuckles he attacks Kirk Jameson before the Invitational qualifier at Season's Beatings on 12th December, taps to Jared Johnson's Carolina Crossface, and ambushes Randy Bumfhole and Fumihiro Ota at End Of Days. In the three-way for the Tag Team titles at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012 he takes a Cal Cutter from Kashmir Singh, and Lockdown are put out of the match and out of the promotion; Andrews tells them they are fired. The narrator reports at the end of January that Shady K has signed for RIPW on a pay-per-appearance deal.

name: Knuckles
caption: The other half of Lockdown, Aaron Andrews's hired muscle, the bigger of the pair. He beats Wanda Fish with a clothesline and a big boot on the night of Remember November, 26th November 2011, to become the All Action champion, and loses the belt to Amazing Fire Fly minutes later, after the Peacekeepers match; the same night he slams Sheriff Blaze on Marshall Dillon and gorilla-presses Shady K. At Season's Beatings on 12th December he breaks a chair across the fallen Kirk Jameson and beats Jonnie Perez and Bradford Peverell with a Stay Of Execution; at End Of Days he takes the Bumfhole Buster from Randy Bumfhole, and he beats the West Texas Peacekeepers with a Knuckle Duster on Sheriff Blaze at New Year, Old Rivalries on 5th January 2012. After Lockdown are fired at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January the narrator reports that he has signed a developmental deal with RIPW to join his long-term partner.

name: Wanda Fish
caption: A woman who has wrestled all over the world and who debuts at Remember November on 26th November 2011 in a hooded sweatshirt as a backstage worker, pins Black Eagle in a pile of chairs to become the All Action champion (the diary's own title records call her the first female champion) and tells the locker room that she is "crossing the gender divide" and expects a lot of challenges; Knuckles takes the belt from her minutes later. At Season's Beatings she beats Citizen X in thirteen minutes with the Dish Of The Day, at End Of Days she beats Nathan Coleman in an Invitational qualifier, and on 5th January 2012 she and Jared Johnson beat the Second Sons, Wanda pinning Antonio. She loses to JD Morgan's Cross Atlantic Stretch in the first round of The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January. The narrator calls her a straight-up tremendous wrestler, and tew.com notes that she has talked openly about retirement. In the diary's pages from February 2012 she makes Thea Davis her protégé and loses with her to Raphael and Citizen X at Leap Into The Unknown, tells the narrator she will retire in a few weeks, loses a Triple Threat for the All Action title to JD Morgan at All Or Nothing and, in her last match, the Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews at Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March, a B- match in which she very nearly won a three-count. The narrator, Rip Chord and others attend her retirement party; he says she cost $3,000 a time.

name: Lassana Makutsi
caption: A newcomer who debuts at Remember November on 26th November 2011 and loses to Roderick Remus in under six minutes, the narrator calling it a promising effort from a worker nobody knows. At Season's Beatings on 12th December he carries Providence through an Invitational qualifier like a seasoned veteran, the narrator praising his understanding of the psychology of a fight, and loses to the Eye Of Providence; he loses to Antonio on the 17th December tour show and to Greg Ford on the 24th, and at End Of Days he and Amazing Fire Fly lose to the Dark Raptors when Makutsi eats a Phoenix Firebird Splash. In January the narrator names him, with Raphael and an undebuted worker, among the works in progress. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he loses to Raphael at All Or Nothing on 12th February, to Providence at Third Time's The Charm, to Primus Allen in a Traditional title match at March Madness on 12th March, in which the narrator finds the two have tremendous chemistry, and, with KC Glenn, to the Second Sons in the Spring Fever three-way. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he loses the Heavyweight title match to Aaron Andrews, who picks him as an easy opponent, at High Noon on 5th June, and then teams with Jared Johnson as Team Honor, whom the narrator says have great chemistry; he loses to Always Breakin' Hollywood and the Second Sons, challenges Black Eagle at Iron on 12th August for the All Action title he calls dishonourably captured, is kicked in the stomach by Eagle and Firebird, and at Back To School on 5th September locks the Carolina Crossface on Eagle to win the Tag Team titles.

name: Nathan Coleman
caption: A short-term signing who arrives without fanfare, in the narrator's words with no sizzle or flash but an economy of movement that can rip apart any opponent in a few moves. At Season's Beatings on 12th December 2011 he and JD Morgan beat Randy Bumfhole and Kid Arachnid, Coleman flattening Arachnid for the pin; at End Of Days he loses an Invitational qualifier to Wanda Fish's Dish Of The Day, and at New Year, Old Rivalries on 5th January 2012 he partners Aaron Andrews, whom he suits as a tag partner, and takes the Bullseye from Kirk Jameson. The narrator's January notes say he was brought in to do a job, did it, and leaves with the company's thanks when his contract runs down.

name: Haley Buck
caption: A "wench" who appears unnamed at Eleventh Hour on 12th November 2011, a sweet-looking girl in a long skirt and high-collared blouse with a skull-and-crossbones earring, as Hugh de Aske's new companion; she tells the Internet Favourites that her client would like to team with Fumihiro Ota, which makes Team OMGsplosion. Named at End Of Days on 26th December, in a power suit with padded shoulders, she tells the crowd that she arranged for Hugh to be fired because he expected her to do his laundry, and aligns herself with JD Morgan as his manager; the narrator notes that her earlier appearance was such a non-event that the heel turn gives her a second chance to make a first impression. She leads Morgan to the ring for The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012 and cheers him on from ringside through the final. In the diary's pages from March to May 2012 she faces down Kashmir Singh backstage at Third Time's The Charm, says Rip has been plotting something for the coming weeks, appears beside JD Morgan before the Gold Rush match at April Showers, where she shouts at him to make the cover on Primus Allen, and shrieks at ringside at South East Crisis and at Mother, May I?. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 she introduces Primus Allen and Lenny Brown at High Noon on 5th June as Always Breakin' Hollywood, her latest clients after a pirate and JD Morgan, and pushes them at South East Madness, Hotter Than Hot, Iron and Back To School, telling the XX Factor on 5th September that she could get them work as extras. She watches Morgan at Summer Showdown, urging him to join The Fallen for the money, hypes him at Hotter Than Hot, and at Summernova on 5th August says that he has dropped her for allying with the Knights Templar and brings out Sean Deeley, whom she manages against Morgan at South East Grand Parade and talks up again at Iron.

name: Dwight Kumas
caption: The referee of the Heavyweight title match between Aaron Andrews and Randy Bumfhole at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012, whom Andrews pulls in front of himself to stop a Bumfhole clothesline. He referees the tag match between KC Glenn and Jared Johnson and the Canadian Blondes at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March 2012.

name: Thea Davis
caption: A flame-haired young woman introduced at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February 2012 as the protégé of Wanda Fish, who has her training on a heavy punch bag and calls her the most talented worker of her age she has seen in years, male or female. The narrator says he had thought of bringing her in under a hood for an eventual reveal and has instead made her Fish's protégé, since Wanda is not getting any younger; as the lowest member of the roster she takes the fall when she and Fish lose to Raphael and Citizen X, pinned with Flaming Anarchy. In March the narrator's survey of the regional companies says that the women's company AAA could cause MAW trouble by taking her, and that, high as he is on her prospects, it would not be a major loss; after Mother, May I? he notes that she has extended her contract with another company. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 she wins the High Noon six-man on 5th June with Bradford Peverell and Jared Johnson, yanking Eddie Powell off the top rope when he stops to flirt with her, and loses to Raphael's Italian DDT at South East Madness on 9th June, an opener the narrator designs to limit costs. At Hotter Than Hot on 5th July she takes a new regular partner, Jaime Quine, as The XX Factor; they lose to Providence and Father Johan, to the Dark Raptors for the Tag Team titles at Summernova on 5th August and to Always Breakin' Hollywood at Back To School on 5th September, where Davis tells interviewer Jenny that they will always try their best.

name: Lord Geoffrey Windameer
caption: A newcomer who makes his first appearance at April Showers on 5th April 2012 in an expensive charcoal suit to classical music, telling the crowd that he would be back at Windameer Manor with his servants but for his family's thirst for competition, that he is their superior socially, historically and physically, and that, as the future lord of the land, he will take care of them from the first. The narrator notes that Windameer is also Paul Huntingdon and Aristocrat, an SWF midcarder like Citizen X who is better matched against uppercarders. He beats Jared Johnson with a High Society at his debut, loses to Kirk Jameson at Spring Fever on 12th April, and in the three-way for the Traditional title at Mother, May I? on 12th May tries to order JD Morgan around, is slapped for it and is put down by Bradford Peverell's Dream Left Hook before Morgan wins. In the diary's pages from June to August 2012 he loses the High Noon six-man on 5th June after the counter-wrestling clinic with Jared Johnson and beats Amazing Fire Fly with a High Society at Iron on 12th August. The narrator's news in June has him, as Paul Huntingdon, winning the SWF Shooting Star title from Hugh de Aske.

name: Donnie J
caption: A high-flyer "of CZCW fame" who makes his first appearance at April Showers on 5th April 2012 with a promise to put the fright into every champion in the company, and beats Citizen X with a Death On Miami Beach in the narrator's "bit too CZCW" match. At South East Crisis on 8th April Rip Chord puts the All Action title in a ladder match and Donnie J, at home among the ladders, hangs from the belt to win it from JD Morgan (the diary's own title records list "Donnie J April 2012 0"). At May The Force Be With You on 5th May he is beaten for it by Aaron Andrews in a title-versus-title match, regains it at Great Lakes Madness on 9th May in a two-out-of-three-falls match ("Donnie J (2) May 2012 7") and at Mother, May I? on 12th May loses the thirty-minute Iron Man match for the Heavyweight title to Andrews by the skin of his teeth. After that show the narrator notes that he has extended his contract with another company. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 the "Dogfight" keeps the All Action title against Father Johan in a pole match at High Noon on 5th June, Firebird in a submission match at South East Madness on 9th June, Eddie Powell and Citizen X at Summer Showdown, Firebird again at Hotter Than Hot, JD Morgan in a thirty-minute draw at Great Lakes Grand Parade, Powell and Rudy Velasquez at Summernova and Providence in a ladder match at South East Grand Parade, where he says he feels he needs to be the one to stop him. He agrees to help the faces against The Fallen only in the ring, loses the belt backstage to Black Eagle at Iron on 12th August and takes it back the same night, hitting Firebird with a metal briefcase; the narrator's news says that he has left 4C as its money troubles mount, and at Back To School on 5th September he loses a six-man with Morgan and Amazing Fire Fly, then stands with Kashmir Singh and Brandon Smith to protect Sienna LeNoir.

name: Lenny Brown
caption: A tall newcomer who slides into the ring at South East Crisis on 8th April 2012 to kick Amazing Fire Fly after Primus Allen has been beaten, and who is introduced by Allen as an old friend from before wrestling; Allen says they are in the hunt for every title in the company. At Spring Fever on 12th April the narrator admits he has been rushed into a top spot alongside Allen and loses to Fumihiro Ota with a Ninja Strike, and at May The Force Be With You on 5th May he and Allen beat Amazing Fire Fly and Ota, Allen pinning Fly with a Sit-Out Spinebuster. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he and Primus Allen are Haley Buck's Always Breakin' Hollywood, Brown crushing Marshall Dillon with The Star Treatment at High Noon on 5th June, and he declares at South East Madness that after Team Honor comes the next challenge and then the Tag Team titles. At Iron on 12th August he names Sean Deeley, himself and Allen as members of the group Buck is putting together and offers Rudy Velasquez a place in it, and at Back To School on 5th September he helps Allen hold both members of the XX Factor for a double spinning side slam.

name: Eddie Powell
caption: A newcomer in a polyester lounge suit and a white man's afro, who comes to the ring to a wailing saxophone at South East Crisis on 8th April 2012 as "the sultan of shimmer, the lord of the lock-in, your god of good times", and tells the locker room to lighten up. The narrator, who writes of having held off hiring "Teddy Powell" because he thought him a lightweight, sees a good start in a loss to Fumihiro Ota's Ninja Strike. At May The Force Be With You on 5th May he is dropped from a doorframe by Bradford Peverell and loses to his Dream Left Hook, and at Mother, May I? on 12th May he beats Jared Johnson with a Motion Sensor. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he loses the High Noon six-man on 5th June after hesitating on the top rope to flirt with Thea Davis, is betrayed by Citizen X in the three-way for the All Action title at Summer Showdown on 12th June and is invited by Sienna LeNoir to his sequin-covered door until KC Glenn steps in, beats Amazing Fire Fly with a Motion Censor at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, is smacked around and left down by Rudy Velasquez in the Summernova three-way on 5th August and, at Back To School on 5th September, wins the six-man with Providence and Sean Deeley.

name: Steve Gumble
caption: A former TCW cowboy, signed a couple of hours before South East Crisis on 8th April 2012, who takes up Aaron Andrews's open challenge on the night and loses to the Twisting Face Crusher after almost thirty minutes in which he had Andrews on the verge of defeat with a suicide dive and a Savate Kick. At Spring Fever on 12th April he draws with Firebird, at May The Force Be With You on 5th May he loses to Father Johan's Crucifix Powerbomb, and at Mother, May I? on 12th May he loses to Providence's Eye Of Providence in a match the narrator says is interlinked with his plans for the masked man. In the diary's pages from June to August 2012 he draws with JD Morgan for the Traditional title at High Noon on 5th June, loses to Morgan at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, beats Citizen X with a Savate Kick at Beach Blast on 12th July, a rare win, and loses to Sean Deeley's Front Choke Lock at Summernova on 5th August, which the narrator says is perhaps his best and is his last match for the company; the narrator's news says that he has been signed away by the SWF.

name: Father Johan
caption: An evil preacher with fiery red hair and a priest's collar, Firebird's "Father" in his address book, whom Firebird calls in at Spring Fever on 12th April 2012 while Black Eagle is incapacitated, and who arrives at May The Force Be With You on 5th May, kisses Firebird's ring on his hand and says Eagle's wound is grievous but survivable. He beats Steve Gumble with a Crucifix Powerbomb that night, KC Glenn at Great Lakes Madness on 9th May after telling him that he would be welcomed into the family, and with Firebird beats KC Glenn and Kirk Jameson at Mother, May I? on 12th May; he drives Sienna LeNoir from the room as a harlot. The narrator writes that he adores the character, having wanted an evil preacher for a while. In the diary's pages from June to July 2012 he loses a pole match to Donnie J at High Noon on 5th June, where he bludgeons Donnie with the title belt, and tells Firebird that The Fallen must recruit; he beats Bradford Peverell with the Crucifix Powerbomb at Summer Showdown on 12th June speaks to the Second Sons about joining, and with Providence beats Thea Davis and Jaime Quine at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July. At Beach Blast on 12th July the lumberjack match with KC Glenn ends when both men fall from the top turnbuckle to the arena floor; the narrator says his MAW career limps to an end, that the character was excellent but the skills mediocre, and that John "Father Johan" Greed has signed with the SWF.

name: Jim Force
caption: A face-painted muscleman, announced by Rip Chord as Aaron Andrews's surprise challenger for the Heavyweight title at March Madness on 12th March 2012, sprinting down to the ring and sliding in to stay on all fours with wild staring eyes. The narrator calls him a former World champion with a name value who "should never be thought" a MAW-appropriate wrestler, and has nothing but good things to say of him; he controls the opening with hard clotheslines and slams, tires, and loses to the Twisting Face Crusher. The narrator's list of regional companies names him among the stars of RIPW.

name: Jaime Quine
caption: A woman wrestler who appears at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July 2012 as Thea Davis's new regular partner, the pair opening with an open challenge that Providence and Father Johan, who finds women fighting men an abhorrence and delights in it, while Providence likes beating people who cannot fight back, take up; Quine falls to an Eye Of Providence at just under ten minutes. The narrator says there is no positive chemistry in the pairing but that he quite likes them as a team, and that they took the beating against his usual rule because they are not getting main-event pushes. As The XX Factor they tell the crowd that they are not out to prove women better than men and are no more girlfriends than Kashmir Singh and Brandon Smith are boyfriends, and at Summernova on 5th August they lose a Tag Team title challenge to the Dark Raptors, Black Eagle putting Quine down with a New Jersey Turnpike; at Back To School on 5th September Primus Allen and Lenny Brown beat them with a double spinning side slam that drives Quine into the mat.

name: Rudy Velasquez
caption: A Latino high-flyer and brawler, raised in a street gang, whom Rip Chord announces at Summernova on 5th August 2012 as a signing of a few hours earlier and debuts in a three-way for the All Action title against Donnie J and Eddie Powell; he wrecks Powell, trades aerial exchanges with the champion and is beaten by Donnie's Death From Miami Beach. The narrator writes that he has been tracking him since day one and that only the company's heavy heel bias then stopped him bringing him in. At Iron on 12th August he turns down Primus Allen and Lenny Brown's offer, made for their manager, to be the "grit" of the group she is putting together, twists Allen to his knees, and loses to JD Morgan's A Shot Of JD in a Traditional title match; at Back To School on 5th September he taps out to Kirk Jameson's Kirkhold in what the narrator calls a compelling match, having said that what he does he does by himself.

name: Sean Deeley
caption: "The Shooter", a technically gifted submission wrestler whom Haley Buck brings to the ring at Summernova on 5th August 2012 after JD Morgan drops her as his manager, with a promise not to stop until Morgan is lying cold at his feet. He beats Steve Gumble with a Front Choke Lock in what the narrator thinks Gumble's best match for MAW, and at South East Grand Parade on 9th August loses a Traditional title match to Morgan's A Shot Of JD in a contest the narrator calls technically excellent, Morgan taking the pin rather than a submission and Haley Buck telling him it proves nothing. Lenny Brown names him as the finesse of the group Buck is putting together with Brown and Primus Allen. At Back To School on 5th September he pins Morgan in the six-man when Morgan rolls back onto his shoulders out of the Front Choke Lock, and challenges him to a submission match at Where It All Begins Again.

name: Kid Toma
caption: A newcomer whom Kirk Jameson promises at Beach Blast on 12th July 2012 as someone brand new to the company, and whom Rip Chord introduces as a former World Tag Team champion from one of the most storied families in wrestling history, "a tough son of a gun" going places; he faces Aaron Andrews for the Heavyweight title in the main event and loses a spirited but sloppy twenty-five-minute match to the Twisting Face Crusher. The narrator says that if it was a try-out he failed, and that the two have no chemistry; Jameson later names Rich Money as the man who funded Toma's appearance, and the narrator's news says that Toma has signed a development deal, so that he was lucky not to sign him long-term.

name: Rich Money
caption: A genuine International star, known as a despicable heel in the SWF, whom the narrator gets from 4C in a trade for Kirk Jameson at $1,800 a time, about two-thirds of an Andrews, for a three-match run. Jameson brings him to the ring to his familiar SWF theme at Summernova on 5th August 2012 as the man who has funded the Knights Templar and the appearance of Kid Toma, and Rip Chord forces Aaron Andrews to accept his challenge: they go thirty minutes to a draw (B+), the narrator's best rating in about nine months, the fans warming to him as a face and to his Money Roll triple suplexes and Life Of Riley spinning Death Valley Driver. At Iron on 12th August he and Jameson beat Andrews and The Great Ota, Money pinning Andrews with the Bank Roll, and at Back To School on 5th September, the last match of his run, he beats Andrews in a non-title steel cage match, the narrator and Rip having left the result to the wrestlers. The narrator notes that he is about thirty percent more popular than Randy Bumfhole or Andrews, that he will leave a big hole in the roster, and that 4C has not put him in so much as an angle.

name: Blue Shift
caption: One half of the masked team Spectrum Infinity, in a black mask streaked with blue, who in the video introducing the team at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July 2012 kicks a bulky man's head nearly off in a club with a somersault kick while Dawn looks on. He takes to the air in the team's low-key debut against the Canadian Blondes, a loss in front of fewer than 500 fans; Spectrum Infinity beat the Blondes at Summernova on 5th August and lose a Tag Team title challenge to the Dark Raptors, in what the narrator calls basically a squash, at Iron on 12th August.

name: Scarlet Strike
caption: The other half of Spectrum Infinity, in a black mask streaked with red, who in the club video at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July 2012 plants the edge of his hand in a man's throat and throws him over the crowd, and who keeps things on the mat in the team's debut loss to the Canadian Blondes. At Iron on 12th August Black Eagle pins him with a New Jersey Turnpike in the Tag Team title match, and afterwards he tries to take the All Action title from Eagle with a roll-up, only for Firebird to make the save.
